;;; $8000: Reset: hardware init and main loop ;;;
;; Entered from the emulation-mode RESET vector. Quiets the SNES (IRQ/NMI/DMA/HDMA off, APU ports cleared,
;;     force blank),
;; switches to native 16-bit mode, builds the OAM-clear routine in RAM at $7F8000, uploads the SPC700 engine
;;     and samples,
;; clears RAM and then runs the main loop forever.
;; Main loop: wait until NMI sets [$10], count a frame in [$13], run the current game mode (GetGameMode),
;;     clear [$10], repeat.
;; Quirk: the RAM routine is generated code: LDA #$F0 followed by 128 STA $0201+4n (every sprite's Y = $F0,
;;     off-screen) and an RTL.
$00:8000 78           SEI                             ; Disable IRQs
$00:8001 9C 00 42     STZ $4200                       ; Disable NMI, IRQ timers and joypad auto-read
$00:8004 9C 0C 42     STZ $420C                       ; Disable HDMA
$00:8007 9C 0B 42     STZ $420B                       ; Disable DMA
$00:800A 9C 40 21     STZ $2140                       ; \
$00:800D 9C 41 21     STZ $2141                       ; |
$00:8010 9C 42 21     STZ $2142                       ; } Clear APU I/O ports $2140-$2143 (silences the SPC700)
$00:8013 9C 43 21     STZ $2143                       ; /
$00:8016 A9 80        LDA #$80                        ; \
$00:8018 8D 00 21     STA $2100                       ; / Force blank (screen off, brightness 0)
$00:801B 18           CLC                             ; \
$00:801C FB           XCE                             ; / Leave 6502 emulation mode (native mode)
$00:801D C2 38        REP #$38                        ; Binary mode; A, X and Y 16-bit
$00:801F A9 00 00     LDA #$0000                      ; \
$00:8022 5B           TCD                             ; / Direct page = $0000 (so [$xx] is WRAM $7E:00xx)
$00:8023 A9 FF 01     LDA #$01FF                      ; \
$00:8026 1B           TCS                             ; / Stack pointer = $01FF
$00:8027 A9 A9 F0     LDA #$F0A9                      ; A = $F0A9: little-endian bytes A9 F0 = opcode LDA #$F0
$00:802A 8F 00 80 7F  STA $7F8000                     ; Start of RAM routine $7F8000: LDA #$F0
$00:802E A2 7D 01     LDX #$017D                      ; X = $017D: offset of the last generated STA (3 bytes each, 128 of them)
$00:8031 A0 FD 03     LDY #$03FD                      ; Y = $03FD: OAM Y-coordinate address of the last sprite ($0201 + 4*127)
$00:8034 A9 8D 00     LDA #$008D                      ; A = $008D: opcode of STA absolute
$00:8037 9F 02 80 7F  STA $7F8002,X                   ; Write the STA opcode (the extra 00 is overwritten next)
$00:803B 98           TYA                             ; A = OAM address for this STA
$00:803C 9F 03 80 7F  STA $7F8003,X                   ; Write the STA operand: address of this sprite's Y byte
$00:8040 38           SEC                             ; \
$00:8041 E9 04 00     SBC #$0004                      ; } Next OAM Y address: Y = Y - 4
$00:8044 A8           TAY                             ; /
$00:8045 CA           DEX                             ; \
$00:8046 CA           DEX                             ; } X -= 3: previous generated instruction
$00:8047 CA           DEX                             ; /
$00:8048 10 EA        BPL $EA [$8034]                 ; Loop for all 128 sprites
$00:804A E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$00:804C A9 6B        LDA #$6B                        ; A = $6B: opcode of RTL
$00:804E 8F 82 81 7F  STA $7F8182                     ; End the RAM routine with RTL at $7F8182
$00:8052 20 E8 80     JSR $80E8                       ; Upload the SPC700 engine (UploadSPCEngine)
$00:8055 9C 00 01     STZ $0100                       ; Game mode = 0 (load Nintendo Presents)
$00:8058 9C 09 01     STZ $0109                       ; Clear [$0109] (level number / intro level flag)
$00:805B 20 4E 8A     JSR $8A4E                       ; Clear $0000-$00FF and $0200-$1FFF and the stripe image buffer (ClearStack)
$00:805E 20 FD 80     JSR $80FD                       ; Upload sample data to the SPC700 (UploadSamples)
$00:8061 20 50 92     JSR $9250                       ; Set up HDMA channel 7 (window effect) and clear its table ($9250)
$00:8064 A9 03        LDA #$03                        ; \
$00:8066 8D 01 21     STA $2101                       ; / OBJ tiles at VRAM $6000, 8x8 and 16x16 sprite sizes
$00:8069 E6 10        INC $10                         ; [$10] = 1: skip the NMI wait on the first pass
$00:806B A5 10        LDA $10                         ; \
$00:806D F0 FC        BEQ $FC [$806B]                 ; / Spin until NMI sets [$10] (frame ready)
$00:806F 58           CLI                             ; Enable IRQs
$00:8070 E6 13        INC $13                         ; Count a frame: [$13]++
$00:8072 20 22 93     JSR $9322                       ; Run the current game mode (GetGameMode)
$00:8075 64 10        STZ $10                         ; \
$00:8077 80 F2        BRA $F2 [$806B]                 ; / [$10] = 0: this frame's game logic is done, wait for the next NMI


; SPC Upload information is here: http://romhack.wikia.com/wiki/Spc700.rom and http://romhacking.net/docs/197/

;;; $8079: Upload data blocks to SPC700 (SPC700UploadLoop) ;;;
;; Sends one or more blocks to the SPC700 through APU ports $2140-$2143 using the IPL boot ROM transfer
;;     protocol.
;; Block format at [$00]: 16-bit length, 16-bit SPC700 destination address, then the data bytes. A block of
;;     length 0 ends the
;; transfer; its address is where the SPC700 starts running.
;; Parameters: [$00]-[$02]: 24-bit ROM address of the first block.
;; Returns: APU ports cleared; processor flags preserved.
$00:8079 08           PHP                             ; Save processor flags
$00:807A C2 30        REP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 16-bit
$00:807C A0 00 00     LDY #$0000                      ; Y = 0: offset into the data at [$00]
$00:807F A9 AA BB     LDA #$BBAA                      ; \
$00:8082 CD 40 21     CMP $2140                       ; } Wait for the SPC700 IPL ROM to signal ready ($BBAA on ports 0/1)
$00:8085 D0 FB        BNE $FB [$8082]                 ; /
$00:8087 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$00:8089 A9 CC        LDA #$CC                        ; A = $CC: IPL start-transfer command
$00:808B 80 26        BRA $26 [$80B3]                 ; Send the command and the block header (first block)

$00:808D B7 00        LDA [$00],Y                     ; Fetch the first data byte of the block
$00:808F C8           INY                             ; Advance the data offset
$00:8090 EB           XBA                             ; Park the byte in the high half of A
$00:8091 A9 00        LDA #$00                        ; Transfer counter = 0 for the first byte
$00:8093 80 0B        BRA $0B [$80A0]                 ; Send it
$00:8095 EB           XBA                             ; \
$00:8096 B7 00        LDA [$00],Y                     ; |
$00:8098 C8           INY                             ; } Next data byte goes in B, transfer counter in A
$00:8099 EB           XBA                             ; /
$00:809A CD 40 21     CMP $2140                       ; \
$00:809D D0 FB        BNE $FB [$809A]                 ; / Wait until the SPC700 echoes the previous counter on port 0
$00:809F 1A           INC A                           ; Counter + 1
$00:80A0 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; \
$00:80A2 8D 40 21     STA $2140                       ; } Port 0 = counter, port 1 = data byte (one 16-bit write)
$00:80A5 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; /
$00:80A7 CA           DEX                             ; \
$00:80A8 D0 EB        BNE $D0 [$8095]                 ; / Repeat for all bytes of the block (X = byte count)
$00:80AA CD 40 21     CMP $2140                       ; \
$00:80AD D0 FB        BNE $FB [$80AA]                 ; / Wait until the SPC700 echoes the last counter
$00:80AF 69 03        ADC #$03                        ; \
$00:80B1 F0 FC        BEQ $FC [$80AF]                 ; / Next block command = counter + 4 (CMP leaves carry set), never 0
$00:80B3 48           PHA                             ; Save the command byte
$00:80B4 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$00:80B6 B7 00        LDA [$00],Y                     ; A = block length
$00:80B8 C8           INY                             ; \
$00:80B9 C8           INY                             ; / Skip the length word
$00:80BA AA           TAX                             ; X = block length
$00:80BB B7 00        LDA [$00],Y                     ; A = block destination address in SPC700 RAM
$00:80BD C8           INY                             ; \
$00:80BE C8           INY                             ; / Skip the address word
$00:80BF 8D 42 21     STA $2142                       ; Send the address to ports 2/3
$00:80C2 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$00:80C4 E0 01 00     CPX #$0001                      ; Carry = 1 if the block has data (length >= 1)
$00:80C7 A9 00        LDA #$00                        ; \
$00:80C9 2A           ROL                             ; } Port 1 = 1 for a data block, 0 for the end block (SPC700 starts running)
$00:80CA 8D 41 21     STA $2141                       ; /
$00:80CD 69 7F        ADC #$7F                        ; V = 1 if the block had data (A = 1 overflows when adding $7F)
$00:80CF 68           PLA                             ; \
$00:80D0 8D 40 21     STA $2140                       ; |
$00:80D3 CD 40 21     CMP $2140                       ; } Send the command byte on port 0 and wait for the SPC700 to echo it
$00:80D6 D0 FB        BNE $FB [$80D3]                 ; /
$00:80D8 70 B3        BVS $B3 [$808D]                 ; Block had data: go send it ($00808D); otherwise finish
$00:80DA 9C 40 21     STZ $2140                       ; \
$00:80DD 9C 41 21     STZ $2141                       ; |
$00:80E0 9C 42 21     STZ $2142                       ; } Clear APU ports 0-3 (end the transfer)
$00:80E3 9C 43 21     STZ $2143                       ; /
$00:80E6 28           PLP                             ; Restore processor flags
$00:80E7 60           RTS                             ; Unused stub: A = 0 (loads zero, no effect here)



;;; $80E8: Upload SPC700 engine (UploadSPCEngine) ;;;
;; Points [$00] at $0E:8000 (SPC700 engine and its initial data) and falls through into UploadDataToSPC.
$00:80E8 A9 00        LDA #$00                        ; \
$00:80EA 8D 00 00     STA $0000                       ; |
$00:80ED A9 80        LDA #$80                        ; |
$00:80EF 8D 01 00     STA $0001                       ; |
$00:80F2 A9 0E        LDA #$0E                        ; } [$00] = $0E8000 (SPC700 engine and initial data)
$00:80F4 8D 02 00     STA $0002                       ; /

;;; $80F7: Upload data with IRQs disabled (UploadDataToSPC) ;;;
;; Wraps SPC700UploadLoop in SEI/CLI because the handshake is timing sensitive.
;; Parameters: [$00]-[$02]: 24-bit ROM address of the data. Note: always leaves IRQs enabled (CLI).
$00:80F7 78           SEI                             ; Disable IRQs: the handshake is timing sensitive
$00:80F8 20 79 80     JSR $8079                       ; Upload the data blocks at [$00]
$00:80FB 58           CLI                             ; Enable IRQs
$00:80FC 60           RTS                             ; Return


;;; $80FD: Upload sample data to SPC700 (UploadSamples) ;;;
;; Points [$00] at $0F:8000 (BRR sample pointers and data) and uploads it via StrtSPCMscUpld.
$00:80FD A9 00        LDA #$00                        ; \
$00:80FF 8D 00 00     STA $0000                       ; |
$00:8102 A9 80        LDA #$80                        ; |
$00:8104 8D 01 00     STA $0001                       ; |
$00:8107 A9 0F        LDA #$0F                        ; } [$00] = $0F8000 (sample pointers and BRR data)
$00:8109 8D 02 00     STA $0002                       ; /
$00:810C 80 0F        BRA $0F [$811D]                 ; Upload it (StrtSPCMscUpld)


;;; $810E: Upload music bank 1 (title, overworld) (UploadMusicBank1) ;;;
;; Points [$00] at $0E:98B1 and falls through into StrtSPCMscUpld. Called when the title screen and the
;;     overworld are loaded.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:96C3: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:A0B3: Game mode 0C: load overworld (LoadMapGameMode)
$00:810E A9 B1        LDA #$B1                        ; \
$00:8110 8D 00 00     STA $0000                       ; |
$00:8113 A9 98        LDA #$98                        ; |
$00:8115 8D 01 00     STA $0001                       ; |
$00:8118 A9 0E        LDA #$0E                        ; } [$00] = $0E98B1 (music bank 1: title and overworld)
$00:811A 8D 02 00     STA $0002                       ; /

;;; $811D: Request and run SPC700 upload (StrtSPCMscUpld) ;;;
;; Common tail of the sample and music uploads. Writes $FF to APU port 1 (probably asks the running SPC700
;;     engine to jump back
;; to its IPL loader), uploads the blocks at [$00], then falls into SPC700ZeroLoop to clear the ports.
;; Parameters: [$00]-[$02]: 24-bit ROM address of the data.
$00:811D A9 FF        LDA #$FF                        ; \
$00:811F 8D 41 21     STA $2141                       ; / Port 1 = $FF: ask the SPC700 engine to accept an upload (probably jumps to the IPL)
$00:8122 20 F7 80     JSR $80F7                       ; Upload the data blocks at [$00] (UploadDataToSPC)
$00:8125 A2 03        LDX #$03                        ; X = 3: clear four ports and mirrors

;;; $8127: Clear APU ports and sound mirrors (SPC700ZeroLoop) ;;;
;; Clears APU I/O ports $2140-$2143 and the RAM mirrors $1DF9-$1E00 (sound requests and last-sent music value
;;     $1DFF).
;; $008134 (entry point from the Mario Start game mode): uploads the level music bank only when [$1425] is
;;     non-zero, [$0109] = $E9,
;; or [$0109], [$141A] and [$141D] are all zero; otherwise returns without uploading.
$00:8127 9E 40 21     STZ $2140,X                     ; Clear APU port X ($2140-$2143)
$00:812A 9E F9 1D     STZ $1DF9,X                     ; Clear sound mirror $1DF9+X
$00:812D 9E FD 1D     STZ $1DFD,X                     ; Clear $1DFD+X (mirrors $1DFD-$1E00, includes last music value $1DFF)
$00:8130 CA           DEX                             ; \
$00:8131 10 F4        BPL SPC700ZeroLoop              ; / X--, loop for X = 3..0
$00:8133 60           RTS                             ; Return

$00:8134 AD 25 14     LDA $1425                       ; Entry from the Mario Start game mode: [$1425] (probably bonus game flag)
$00:8137 D0 0F        BNE UploadMusicBank2            ; Non-zero: upload level music
$00:8139 AD 09 01     LDA $0109                       ; A = [$0109] (level-load flag)
$00:813C C9 E9        CMP #$E9                        ; [$0109] = $E9 (special value)?
$00:813E F0 08        BEQ UploadMusicBank2            ; Yes: upload level music
$00:8140 0D 1A 14     ORA $141A                       ; \
$00:8143 0D 1D 14     ORA $141D                       ; } Skip the upload if [$0109], [$141A] or [$141D] is non-zero (probably music already loaded)
$00:8146 D0 EB        BNE $008133                     ; /

;;; $8148: Upload music bank 2 (levels) (UploadMusicBank2) ;;;
;; Points [$00] at $0E:AED6 (level music) and jumps to StrtSPCMscUpld.
$00:8148 A9 D6        LDA #$D6                        ; \
$00:814A 8D 00 00     STA $0000                       ; |
$00:814D A9 AE        LDA #$AE                        ; |
$00:814F 8D 01 00     STA $0001                       ; |
$00:8152 A9 0E        LDA #$0E                        ; } [$00] = $0EAED6 (music bank 2: level music)
$00:8154 8D 02 00     STA $0002                       ; /
$00:8157 80 C4        BRA StrtSPCMscUpld              ; Upload it (StrtSPCMscUpld)


;;; $8159: Upload music bank 3 (ending) (UploadMusicBank3) ;;;
;; Points [$00] at $03:E400 (ending/credits music) and jumps to StrtSPCMscUpld.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:94A0: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
$00:8159 A9 00        LDA #$00                        ; \
$00:815B 8D 00 00     STA $0000                       ; |
$00:815E A9 E4        LDA #$E4                        ; |
$00:8160 8D 01 00     STA $0001                       ; |
$00:8163 A9 03        LDA #$03                        ; } [$00] = $03E400 (music bank 3: ending music)
$00:8165 8D 02 00     STA $0002                       ; /
$00:8168 80 B3        BRA StrtSPCMscUpld              ; Upload it (StrtSPCMscUpld)


;;; $816A: NMI handler: sound, PPU mirrors, DMA (NMIStart) ;;;
;; Runs once per frame at the start of V-blank. Saves registers, delivers queued music/SFX requests to the
;;     SPC700, forces blank,
;; copies the window/color-math mirrors [$41]-[$44] to the PPU, then does all VRAM/CGRAM/OAM DMA and reads the
;;     controllers.
;; Lag detection: [$10] is cleared by the main loop when it finishes a frame. If [$10] is still non-zero on
;;     entry the game logic
;; overran the frame (lag), so the heavy DMA work is skipped and only scroll registers are updated.
;; [$0D9B] (special level mode): bit 7 set sends control to the Mode 7 boss room path at $0082C4. Falls into
;;     NMINotSpecialLv.
$00:816A 78           SEI                             ; Disable IRQs
$00:816B 08           PHP                             ; Save processor flags
$00:816C C2 30        REP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 16-bit
$00:816E 48           PHA                             ; \
$00:816F DA           PHX                             ; |
$00:8170 5A           PHY                             ; } Save A, X, Y and the data bank
$00:8171 8B           PHB                             ; /
$00:8172 4B           PHK                             ; \
$00:8173 AB           PLB                             ; / Data bank = program bank ($00)
$00:8174 E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$00:8176 AD 10 42     LDA $4210                       ; Acknowledge NMI (read RDNMI)
$00:8179 AD FB 1D     LDA $1DFB                       ; \
$00:817C D0 08        BNE $008186                     ; / Music request pending in [$1DFB]? Then go send it
$00:817E AC 42 21     LDY $2142                       ; \
$00:8181 CC FF 1D     CPY $1DFF                       ; } Y = APU port 2; if it differs from last sent music value [$1DFF], skip to SFX
$00:8184 D0 09        BNE $00818F                     ; /
$00:8186 8D 42 21     STA $2142                       ; \
$00:8189 8D FF 1D     STA $1DFF                       ; } Port 2 = request (or 0 once echoed), remember it in [$1DFF], clear [$1DFB]
$00:818C 9C FB 1D     STZ $1DFB                       ; /
$00:818F AD F9 1D     LDA $1DF9                       ; \
$00:8192 8D 40 21     STA $2140                       ; / APU port 0 = [$1DF9] (sound effect request)
$00:8195 AD FA 1D     LDA $1DFA                       ; \
$00:8198 8D 41 21     STA $2141                       ; / APU port 1 = [$1DFA] (sound effect request)
$00:819B AD FC 1D     LDA $1DFC                       ; \
$00:819E 8D 43 21     STA $2143                       ; / APU port 3 = [$1DFC] (sound effect request)
$00:81A1 9C F9 1D     STZ $1DF9                       ; \
$00:81A4 9C FA 1D     STZ $1DFA                       ; } Clear the three sound effect mirrors
$00:81A7 9C FC 1D     STZ $1DFC                       ; /
$00:81AA A9 80        LDA #$80                        ; \
$00:81AC 8D 00 21     STA $2100                       ; / Force blank while VRAM, CGRAM and OAM are updated
$00:81AF 9C 0C 42     STZ $420C                       ; Disable HDMA (re-enabled from [$0D9F] at the end of NMI)
$00:81B2 A5 41        LDA $41                         ; \
$00:81B4 8D 23 21     STA $2123                       ; / W12SEL = [$41] (BG1/BG2 window mask)
$00:81B7 A5 42        LDA $42                         ; \
$00:81B9 8D 24 21     STA $2124                       ; / W34SEL = [$42] (BG3/BG4 window mask)
$00:81BC A5 43        LDA $43                         ; \
$00:81BE 8D 25 21     STA $2125                       ; / WOBJSEL = [$43] (OBJ/color window mask)
$00:81C1 A5 44        LDA $44                         ; \
$00:81C3 8D 30 21     STA $2130                       ; / CGWSEL = [$44] (color math control)

$00:822D 88           DEY                             ; |

$00:82A4 9C 11 21     STZ.W $2111                     ; \
$00:82A7 9C 11 21     STZ.W $2111                     ; |
$00:82AA 9C 12 21     STZ.W $2112                     ; } BG3 H and V scroll = 0 (status bar does not scroll)
$00:82AD 9C 12 21     STZ.W $2112                     ; /

$00:82C8 E6 10        INC $10                         ; Mark the frame handled: [$10]++
$00:82CA AD 3A 14     LDA.W $143A                     ; \

$00:82F7 A9 09        LDA.B #$09                      ; \

$00:82FC A5 2A        LDA $2A                         ; \

$00:8308 8D 1F 21     STA.W $211F                     ; /

$00:8315 69 00        ADC.B #$00                      ; } Mode 7 center Y = [$2C]/[$2D] + $0080

$00:8345 AD 9B 0D     LDA.W $0D9B                     ; \

$00:8349 90 11        BCC $835C                       ; /
$00:834B AD AE 0D     LDA.W $0DAE                     ; \
$00:834E 8D 00 21     STA.W $2100                     ; / INIDISP = [$0DAE]: brightness
$00:8351 AD 9F 0D     LDA.W $0D9F                     ; \

$00:8357 A9 81        LDA.B #$81                      ; \

;;; $8374: IRQ vector entry (IRQHandler) ;;;
;; Masks further IRQs and falls into IRQStart.
$00:8374 78           SEI                             ; Mask further IRQs

;;; $8375: IRQ: save registers, check timer (IRQStart) ;;;
;; Saves state, acknowledges the IRQ via $4211 and ignores it unless the V-count timer fired. Bit 7 of [$0D9B]
;;     set sends control
;; to the Mode 7 boss room IRQ code at $0083BA. Otherwise falls into IRQNMIEnding.
$00:8375 08           PHP                             ; Save processor flags
$00:8376 C2 30        REP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 16-bit
$00:8378 48           PHA                             ; \
$00:8379 DA           PHX                             ; |
$00:837A 5A           PHY                             ; } Save A, X, Y and the data bank
$00:837B 8B           PHB                             ; /
$00:837C 4B           PHK                             ; \
$00:837D AB           PLB                             ; / Data bank = program bank ($00)
$00:837E E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$00:8380 AD 11 42     LDA.W $4211                     ; Read TIMEUP: acknowledges the IRQ, bit 7 = V-count timer fired
$00:8383 10 2D        BPL $83B2                       ; Timer did not fire: just restore registers and return

$00:8387 AC 9B 0D     LDY.W $0D9B                     ; Y = [$0D9B] (special level mode)

;;; $838C: IRQ: set BG3 scroll and screen mode (IRQNMIEnding) ;;;

;;     BGMODE from [$3E]
;; and CGADSUB from [$40] for the part of the screen below the status bar. Restores registers and falls into
;;     the RTI.

$00:8394 A5 22        LDA $22                         ; \
$00:8396 8D 11 21     STA.W $2111                     ; |
$00:8399 A5 23        LDA $23                         ; } BG3 H-scroll = [$22]/[$23]
$00:839B 8D 11 21     STA.W $2111                     ; /
$00:839E A5 24        LDA $24                         ; \
$00:83A0 8D 12 21     STA.W $2112                     ; |

$00:83B5 7A           PLY                             ; |
$00:83B6 FA           PLX                             ; |
$00:83B7 68           PLA                             ; } Restore registers and flags
$00:83B8 28           PLP                             ; /

;;; $83B9: IRQ return and Mode 7 boss splits (EmptyHandler) ;;;

;; $0083BA: IRQ path for Mode 7 boss rooms. Iggy/Larry ([$0D9B] bit 6 clear) use a single split that switches
;;     to Mode 7 below the
;; status bar. Others use two stages counted in [$11]: stage 0 programs a second V-count IRQ at line $AE -
;;     [$1888] and enters Mode 7;

$00:83BA 2C 9B 0D     BIT.W $0D9B                     ; \

$00:83BF A4 11        LDY $11                         ; \

$00:83C3 8D 00 42     STA.W $4200                     ; Second stage: NMITIMEN = $81, no more IRQs
$00:83C6 A0 14        LDY.B #$14                      ; Y = $14: delay count

$00:83D0 E6 11        INC $11                         ; IRQ stage [$11] = 1

$00:83DB 8D 09 42     STA.W $4209                     ; /
$00:83DE 9C 0A 42     STZ.W $420A                     ; V-count timer high = 0
$00:83E1 A9 A1        LDA.B #$A1                      ; A = $A1: NMI, V-count IRQ and joypad auto-read
$00:83E3 AC 93 14     LDY.W $1493                     ; \
$00:83E6 F0 0B        BEQ $83F3                       ; / [$1493] (end-of-level timer) = 0: go to $0083F3
$00:83E8 AC 95 14     LDY.W $1495                     ; \

$00:83ED 90 04        BCC $83F3                       ; /

$00:83FD 8D 05 21     STA.W $2105                     ; / BGMODE = $07: Mode 7
$00:8400 A5 3A        LDA $3A                         ; \
$00:8402 8D 0D 21     STA.W $210D                     ; |
$00:8405 A5 3B        LDA $3B                         ; } BG1 H-scroll = [$3A]/[$3B] (Mode 7 scroll)
$00:8407 8D 0D 21     STA.W $210D                     ; /
$00:840A A5 3C        LDA $3C                         ; \
$00:840C 8D 0E 21     STA.W $210E                     ; |
$00:840F A5 3D        LDA $3D                         ; } BG1 V-scroll = [$3C]/[$3D] (Mode 7 scroll)
$00:8411 8D 0E 21     STA.W $210E                     ; /
$00:8414 80 9C        BRA $83B2                       ; Restore registers and return ($0083B2)

$00:8430 8D 0E 21     STA.W $210E                     ; /
$00:8433 A5 1D        LDA RAM_ScreenBndryYHi          ; \
$00:8435 8D 0E 21     STA.W $210E                     ; / BG1 V-scroll high = [$1D]
$00:8438 60           RTS                             ; Return

$00:8439 A0 20        LDY.B #$20                      ; Y = $20: delay count (entry point for WaitForHBlank)

;;; $843B: Wait for H-blank, then delay (WaitForHBlank) ;;;
;; Polls HVBJOY ($4212) bit 6. If already in H-blank, retries with Y = $20 (overwriting Y); once H-blank
;;     begins, burns Y loop
;; iterations (DEY/BNE, 5 cycles each) so the caller's PPU writes land at a consistent point in the scanline.
;; Parameters: Y: delay loop count (entry at $008439 uses $20).
;; Called by:
;;     $00:8391: IRQ: set BG3 scroll and screen mode (IRQNMIEnding)
;;     $00:83C8: IRQ return and Mode 7 boss splits (EmptyHandler)
$00:843B 2C 12 42     BIT.W $4212                     ; Read HVBJOY; V flag = bit 6 (H-blank)
$00:843E 70 F9        BVS $8439                       ; Already in H-blank: restart with Y = $20
$00:8440 2C 12 42     BIT.W $4212                     ; Read HVBJOY
$00:8443 50 FB        BVC $8440                       ; Not in H-blank yet: keep polling
$00:8445 88           DEY                             ; \
$00:8446 D0 FD        BNE $8445                       ; / Delay: loop until Y = 0
$00:8448 60           RTS                             ; Return


;;; $8449: DMA OAM buffer to OAM (DoSomeSpriteDMA) ;;;
;; Copies the $0220-byte OAM shadow buffer at $00:0200 to OAM using DMA channel 0, then sets OAM address to
;;     [$3F]
;; with priority rotation on, so the sprite at that index has highest priority.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:8240: NMI handler: sound, PPU mirrors, DMA (NMIStart)
;;     $00:82F1: NMI tail: scroll, IRQ setup, Mode 7 path (NMINotSpecialLv)
;;     $00:8646: Upload stripe image to VRAM (LoadScrnImage)
$00:8449 9C 00 43     STZ.W $4300                     ; DMA channel 0: mode 0 (single register write)
$00:844C C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$00:844E 9C 02 21     STZ.W $2102                     ; OAM address = 0
$00:8451 A9 04 00     LDA.W #$0004                    ; \
$00:8454 8D 01 43     STA.W $4301                     ; / B-bus register = $04 (OAMDATA)
$00:8457 A9 02 00     LDA.W #$0002                    ; \
$00:845A 8D 03 43     STA.W $4303                     ; / Source address = $00:0200 (OAM shadow buffer)
$00:845D A9 20 02     LDA.W #$0220                    ; \
$00:8460 8D 05 43     STA.W $4305                     ; / Byte count = $0220 (whole OAM)
$00:8463 A0 01        LDY.B #$01                      ; \
$00:8465 8C 0B 42     STY.W $420B                     ; / Start DMA channel 0
$00:8468 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$00:846A A9 80        LDA.B #$80                      ; \
$00:846C 8D 03 21     STA.W $2103                     ; / OAMADDH = $80: sprite priority rotation on
$00:846F A5 3F        LDA $3F                         ; \
$00:8471 8D 02 21     STA.W $2102                     ; / OAMADDL = [$3F]: sets which sprite has highest priority
$00:8474 60           RTS                             ; Return



;;; $8475..848D: Table: OAM size table offsets ;;;
;; Offsets into the $0420 table for $8494: 8 per step, read with an 8-bit index Y = 0,2,4..$1E. Odd
;;     bytes are zero padding.
$00:8475              .db $00,$00,$08,$00,$10,$00,$18,$00 ; $00-$06: offsets $00, $08, $10, $18
$00:847D              .db $20,$00,$28,$00,$30,$00,$38,$00 ; $08-$0E: offsets $20, $28, $30, $38
$00:8485              .db $40,$00,$48,$00,$50,$00,$58,$00 ; $10-$16: offsets $40, $48, $50, $58
$00:848D              .db $60,$00,$68,$00,$70,$00,$78 ; $18-$1E: offsets $60, $68, $70, $78


;;; $8494: Pack OAM size bits into high table ;;;
;; Packs the one-byte-per-sprite size/X-high table at $0420-$049F (values 0-3) into the 2-bits-per-sprite OAM
;;     high table at
;; $0400-$041F: byte = s3<<6 | s2<<4 | s1<<2 | s0, four sprites per byte. 16 iterations of two output bytes
;;     each.
;; $0084C8: long-call wrapper (RTL) that sets the data bank to $00 and runs LoadScrnImage; called from bank
;;     $0C.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:91E6: Mario Start text and level setup helpers
;;     $00:9554: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:955B: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:95B9: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:963A: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:9683: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:97B9: Game mode 11: Mario Start, level music (MarioStartGameMode)
;;     $00:A16D: Game mode 0C: load overworld (LoadMapGameMode)
;;     $00:A1CB: Clear RAM; game mode 0E: overworld (Clear_1A_13D3)
;;     $00:A2F0: Game mode 14: in level (InLevelGameMode)
;;     $00:A5F3: Game mode 12: prepare level (GM04Load)
$00:8494 A0 1E        LDY.B #$1E                      ; Y = $1E: index of the last two output bytes
$00:8496 BE 75 84     LDX.W $8475,Y                   ; X = 4*Y: offset of this group of 8 sprites in $0420 (8-bit index)
$00:8499 BD 23 04     LDA.W $0423,X                   ; \
$00:849C 0A           ASL                             ; |
$00:849D 0A           ASL                             ; |
$00:849E 1D 22 04     ORA.W $0422,X                   ; |
$00:84A1 0A           ASL                             ; |
$00:84A2 0A           ASL                             ; |
$00:84A3 1D 21 04     ORA.W $0421,X                   ; |
$00:84A6 0A           ASL                             ; |
$00:84A7 0A           ASL                             ; } A = [$0420+X..$0423+X] packed 2 bits each, entry X in bits 0-1
$00:84A8 1D 20 04     ORA.W $0420,X                   ; /
$00:84AB 99 00 04     STA.W $0400,Y                   ; Store in OAM high table byte [$0400+Y]
$00:84AE BD 27 04     LDA.W $0427,X                   ; \
$00:84B1 0A           ASL                             ; |
$00:84B2 0A           ASL                             ; |
$00:84B3 1D 26 04     ORA.W $0426,X                   ; |
$00:84B6 0A           ASL                             ; |
$00:84B7 0A           ASL                             ; |
$00:84B8 1D 25 04     ORA.W $0425,X                   ; |
$00:84BB 0A           ASL                             ; |
$00:84BC 0A           ASL                             ; } A = [$0424+X..$0427+X] packed 2 bits each, entry X+4 in bits 0-1
$00:84BD 1D 24 04     ORA.W $0424,X                   ; /
$00:84C0 99 01 04     STA.W $0401,Y                   ; Store in OAM high table byte [$0401+Y]
$00:84C3 88           DEY                             ; \
$00:84C4 88           DEY                             ; } Y -= 2; loop for all 16 pairs
$00:84C5 10 CF        BPL $8496                       ; /
$00:84C7 60           RTS                             ; Return

$00:84C8 8B           PHB                             ; \
$00:84C9 4B           PHK                             ; } Data bank = program bank (old bank saved)
$00:84CA AB           PLB                             ; /
$00:84CB 20 D2 85     JSR.W LoadScrnImage             ; Upload the stripe image selected by [$12] (LoadScrnImage)
$00:84CE AB           PLB                             ; Restore the data bank
$00:84CF 6B           RTL                             ; Return long



;;; $84D0: Pointer table: stripe images (ImagePointers) ;;;

;;     fills itself.

;;; $85D2: Upload stripe image to VRAM (LoadScrnImage) ;;;
;; Loads the 24-bit pointer for image [$12] from ImagePointers into [$00] and uploads it with $871E.
;;     Runs every NMI.
;; If [$12] = 0 (the RAM buffer at $7F:837D) the buffer is emptied afterwards: write index $7F:837B = 0, first
;;     byte = $FF.
;; [$12] is cleared so that an image is only loaded once.
;; Image record format (parsed by $871E): VRAM address high, low, then a word (bit 7 = vertical
;;     increment, bit 6 = RLE, low
;; 14 bits = byte count - 1), then the data. A record whose first byte has bit 7 set ends the image.
;; $0085FA (separate routine, called at the start of most game modes): turns off NMI/IRQ/HDMA and the screen
;;     (TurnOffIO), fills the
;; BG3 tilemap (VRAM $5000-$5FFF) with tile $FC / attributes $38, hides all sprites via $7F8000 and DMAs OAM.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:823D: NMI handler: sound, PPU mirrors, DMA (NMIStart)
;;     $00:82EE: NMI tail: scroll, IRQ setup, Mode 7 path (NMINotSpecialLv)
;;     $00:84CB: Pack OAM size bits into high table
;;     $00:949D: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:94BC: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:94C3: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:9618: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:967C: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:9A10: Boss room tile animation and Mode 7 setup
;;     $00:9A9B: Detect connected controllers into [$0DA0] (SetUp0DA0GM4)
;;     $00:A157: Game mode 0C: load overworld (LoadMapGameMode)
;;     $00:A15E: Game mode 0C: load overworld (LoadMapGameMode)
;;     ... and 1 more
$00:85D2 A4 12        LDY $12                         ; Y = [$12]: byte offset into ImagePointers (image number * 3)
$00:85D4 B9 D0 84     LDA.W ImagePointers,Y           ; \
$00:85D7 85 00        STA $00                         ; / [$00] = pointer low byte
$00:85D9 B9 D1 84     LDA.W ImagePointers+1,Y         ; \
$00:85DC 85 01        STA $01                         ; / [$01] = pointer high byte
$00:85DE B9 D2 84     LDA.W ImagePointers+2,Y         ; \
$00:85E1 85 02        STA $02                         ; / [$02] = pointer bank
$00:85E3 20 1E 87     JSR.W $871E                     ; Upload the stripe image to VRAM ($871E)
$00:85E6 A5 12        LDA $12                         ; \
$00:85E8 D0 0D        BNE $85F7                       ; / [$12] != 0: not the RAM buffer, go to $0085F7
$00:85EA 8F 7B 83 7F  STA.L $7F837B                   ; RAM buffer write index low ($7F:837B) = 0
$00:85EE 8F 7C 83 7F  STA.L $7F837C                   ; RAM buffer write index high ($7F:837C) = 0
$00:85F2 3A           DEC A                           ; A = $FF: end-of-image marker
$00:85F3 8F 7D 83 7F  STA.L $7F837D                   ; First byte of the RAM buffer = $FF (buffer empty)
$00:85F7 64 12        STZ $12                         ; [$12] = 0: do not reload the same image next frame
$00:85F9 60           RTS                             ; Return

$00:85FA 20 7D 93     JSR.W TurnOffIO                 ; Turn off NMI/IRQ, HDMA and the screen (TurnOffIO)
$00:85FD A9 FC        LDA.B #$FC                      ; \
$00:85FF 85 00        STA $00                         ; / [$00] = $FC: tile number used as the fill byte
$00:8601 9C 15 21     STZ.W $2115                     ; VMAIN = 0: VRAM address increments after low-byte writes
$00:8604 9C 16 21     STZ.W $2116                     ; \
$00:8607 A9 50        LDA.B #$50                      ; } VRAM address = $5000 (BG3 tilemap)
$00:8609 8D 17 21     STA.W $2117                     ; /
$00:860C A2 06        LDX.B #$06                      ; \
$00:860E BD 49 86     LDA.W $8649,X                   ; |
$00:8611 9D 10 43     STA.W $4310,X                   ; } Copy 7 bytes of DMA setup from $8649 to $4310-$4316
$00:8614 CA           DEX                             ; |
$00:8615 10 F7        BPL $860E                       ; /
$00:8617 A0 02        LDY.B #$02                      ; \
$00:8619 8C 0B 42     STY.W $420B                     ; / Start DMA channel 1: fill VRAM low bytes with [$00] ($1000 bytes)
$00:861C A9 38        LDA.B #$38                      ; \
$00:861E 85 00        STA $00                         ; / [$00] = $38: fill byte for the high bytes (palette 6, priority)
$00:8620 A9 80        LDA.B #$80                      ; \
$00:8622 8D 15 21     STA.W $2115                     ; / VMAIN = $80: VRAM address increments after high-byte writes
$00:8625 9C 16 21     STZ.W $2116                     ; \
$00:8628 A9 50        LDA.B #$50                      ; } VRAM address = $5000 (BG3 tilemap)
$00:862A 8D 17 21     STA.W $2117                     ; /
$00:862D A2 06        LDX.B #$06                      ; \
$00:862F BD 49 86     LDA.W $8649,X                   ; |
$00:8632 9D 10 43     STA.W $4310,X                   ; } Copy 7 bytes of DMA setup from $8649 to $4310-$4316
$00:8635 CA           DEX                             ; |
$00:8636 10 F7        BPL $862F                       ; /

;;; $8650: Read joypads, update input bytes (ControllerUpdate) ;;;
;; Reads both joypads from the auto-read registers $4218-$421B and keeps held and newly pressed bits for each
;;     in $0DA2-$0DAD.

;;     AXLR, [$18] pressed AXLR.

;;     else the current player [$0DB3].

;;     hides sprites 100-127.

$00:8653 29 F0        AND.B #$F0                      ; Keep only the four button bits
$00:8655 8D A4 0D     STA.W $0DA4                     ; [$0DA4] = joypad 1 A/X/L/R held

$00:8668 8D A2 0D     STA.W $0DA2                     ; [$0DA2] = joypad 1 B/Y/Sel/Start/D-pad held
$00:866B A8           TAY                             ; Y = held bits
$00:866C 4D AA 0D     EOR.W $0DAA                     ; \
$00:866F 2D A2 0D     AND.W $0DA2                     ; |
$00:8672 8D A6 0D     STA.W RAM_OWControllerA         ; / [$0DA6] (RAM_OWControllerA) = joypad 1 byte 1 newly pressed
$00:8675 8C AA 0D     STY.W $0DAA                     ; [$0DAA] = held bits, remembered for next frame

$00:8680 A8           TAY                             ; Y = held bits

$00:868D AD 1B 42     LDA.W $421B                     ; Joypad 2 auto-read high byte

$00:8693 A8           TAY                             ; Y = held bits
$00:8694 4D AB 0D     EOR.W $0DAB                     ; \
$00:8697 2D A3 0D     AND.W $0DA3                     ; |
$00:869A 8D A7 0D     STA.W $0DA7                     ; / [$0DA7] = joypad 2 byte 1 newly pressed
$00:869D 8C AB 0D     STY.W $0DAB                     ; [$0DAB] = held bits, remembered for next frame

;;; JSL trampoline
;;; precondition that A, X, Y are 8-bit registers
;;; takes A = index/2 to table
;;; destroys RAM $00..$03
;;; preserves X, Y, RAM $04..$0f
;;;
;;; [Usage]
;;;     JSL ExecutePtr
;;;     .db $nn, $mm    ; jump $mmnn if A == 0
;;;     .db $nn, $mm    ; jump $mmnn if A == 1
;;;     .db $nn, $mm    ; jump $mmnn if A == 2
;;;     ...
;;; [Alternative]
;;;     JMP (MyTable,X)
;;;   MyTable:
;;;     .db $nn, $mm    ; jump $mmnn if X == 0
;;;     .db $nn, $mm    ; jump $mmnn if X == 2
;;;     .db $nn, $mm    ; jump $mmnn if X == 4
;;;     ...
;;;
;;; Jumps to an address in a table. The accumulator A selects the address.
;;;
;;; ExecutePtr is a trampoline, not a subroutine. This trampoline never returns. The JSL pushes the
;;; long address of the table minus 1; this trampoline pulls it to find the table.
;;;
;;; JMP (MyTable,X) is better than JSL ExecutePtr in new code. The trampoline might be a port from
;;; the 6502 (the processor in the NES). The only JMP instructions of the 6502 were JMP $mmnn and
;;; JMP ($mmnn); there was no JMP ($mmnn,X). The base hack of SMW was Super Mario Bros. 3 (NES); I
;;; wonder if a search for "7a 84 00 0a a8" would find the trampoline in SMB3. When the hackers at
;;; Nintendo ported code from SMB3 to the 65816, a port of the trampoline would have been easier
;;; than a replacement of the trampoline with JMP (MyTable,X).
;;;

;;; $86DF: JSL trampoline: 16-bit pointer table (ExecutePtr) ;;;
;; Jumps to the A-th 16-bit pointer of the table that follows the JSL. Never returns to the caller; the target
;;     returns instead.
;; Parameters: A: table index. 8-bit A, X, Y. Destroys [$00]-[$03]; Y is preserved.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:9325: Run current game mode (GetGameMode)
;;     $00:9B89: Game mode 09: erase file menu
;;     $00:BFC5: Generate Map16 tile at block position (GenerateTile)
;;     $00:C595: Per-frame Mario state: keyhole, timers, animation
;;     $01:8133: Run sprite by status (HandleSprite)
;;     $01:8179: Initialize sprite (CallSpriteInit)
;;     $01:85C8: Dispatch sprite main routine (CallSpriteMain)
;;     $01:AEB9: Thwomp main (Thwomp)
;;     $01:BDE6: Magikoopa main (Magikoopa)
;;     $01:C550: Run power-up action (NoItem)
;;     $01:CE0E: Morton, Roy and Ludwig main routine (WallKoopaKids)
;;     $01:CE61: Pointer table: wall Koopa Kid main states (MortonPtrs1)
;;     ... and 54 more
$00:86DF 84 03        STY $03                         ; Save Y in [$03] (the stack holds the return address)
;;
;; JSL ExecutePtr pushes return address - 1 to the stack. The stack grows down,
;; so we pull the low byte, then the high byte, then the bank byte.
;;
$00:86E1 7A           PLY                             ; \
$00:86E2 84 00        STY $00                         ; / [$00] = low byte of the pushed return address (table address - 1)
$00:86E4 C2 30        REP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 16-bit
$00:86E6 29 FF 00     AND.W #$00FF                    ; Clear the high byte of the index
$00:86E9 0A           ASL                             ; \
$00:86EA A8           TAY                             ; / Y = index * 2 (2-byte table entries)
$00:86EB 68           PLA                             ; \
$00:86EC 85 01        STA $01                         ; / [$01]-[$02] = high and bank bytes of the table address - 1
$00:86EE C8           INY                             ; Y += 1: the pushed address points one byte before the table
$00:86EF B7 00        LDA [$00],Y                     ; \
$00:86F1 85 00        STA $00                         ; / [$00]-[$01] = table entry (16-bit target address)
$00:86F3 E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$00:86F5 A4 03        LDY $03                         ; Restore Y
$00:86F7 DC 00 00     JMP [$0000]                     ; Jump to the target (same bank as the table)

$00:8A24              .db $01,$18,$66,$1C,$00,$40,$00 ; Layer 1 part 3: source $00:1C66, $0040 bytes

$00:8A2B              .db $01,$18,$A6,$1C,$00,$2C,$00 ; Layer 1 part 4: source $00:1CA6, $002C bytes

$00:8A39              .db $01,$18,$28,$1D,$00,$2C,$00 ; Layer 2 part 2: source $00:1D28, $002C bytes

;;; $8A4E: Clear RAM except the stack page (ClearStack) ;;;
;; Clears $0000-$00FF and $0200-$1FFF (the stack page $0100-$01FF is skipped, despite the label), empties the
;;     stripe image buffer at $7F:837B/837D
;; and clears [$0681]. Called at reset and from the game mode loaders.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:96B1: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
$00:8A4E C2 30        REP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 16-bit
$00:8A50 A2 FE 1F     LDX.W #$1FFE                    ; X = $1FFE: top word of the RAM to clear
$00:8A53 74 00        STZ $00,X                       ; Clear the word at $0000+X
$00:8A55 CA           DEX                             ; \
$00:8A56 CA           DEX                             ; / X -= 2
$00:8A57 E0 FF 01     CPX.W #$01FF                    ; \
$00:8A5A 10 05        BPL $8A61                       ; / X >= $01FF: go to the end test at $008A61
$00:8A5C E0 00 01     CPX.W #$0100                    ; \
$00:8A5F 10 F4        BPL $8A55                       ; / $0100 <= X < $01FF (the stack page): skip it without clearing
$00:8A61 E0 FE FF     CPX.W #$FFFE                    ; \
$00:8A64 D0 ED        BNE $8A53                       ; / Loop until X wraps below 0
$00:8A66 A9 00 00     LDA.W #$0000                    ; \
$00:8A69 8F 7B 83 7F  STA.L $7F837B                   ; / $7F:837B = 0: stripe image buffer write index
$00:8A6D 9C 81 06     STZ.W $0681                     ; [$0681] = 0: probably empties the queued palette upload
$00:8A70 E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$00:8A72 A9 FF        LDA.B #$FF                      ; \
$00:8A74 8F 7D 83 7F  STA.L $7F837D                   ; / $7F:837D = $FF: stripe image buffer starts with the end marker
$00:8A78 60           RTS                             ; Return


;;; $8A79: Reset PPU layer addresses and effects (SetUpScreen) ;;;
;; Resets SETINI and mosaic, sets the BG1/BG2/BG3 tilemap sizes and addresses and the chr bases, clears the
;;     window masks and logic (and their RAM mirrors
;; [$41]-[$43]), sets the color math mirror [$44] = $02 and the Mode 7 screen-over mode.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:9394: Game mode 00: load Nintendo Presents (NintendoTile)
;;     $00:946E: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:95C7: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:9643: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:A0B6: Game mode 0C: load overworld (LoadMapGameMode)
;;     $00:A5A5: Game mode 12: prepare level (GM04Load)
$00:8A79 9C 33 21     STZ.W $2133                     ; SETINI = 0: no interlace, no pseudo-hires, no overscan
$00:8A7C 9C 06 21     STZ.W $2106                     ; MOSAIC = 0: mosaic off
$00:8A7F A9 23        LDA.B #$23                      ; \
$00:8A81 8D 07 21     STA.W $2107                     ; / BG1 tilemap at VRAM $2000, 64x64
$00:8A84 A9 33        LDA.B #$33                      ; \
$00:8A86 8D 08 21     STA.W $2108                     ; / BG2 tilemap at VRAM $3000, 64x64
$00:8A89 A9 53        LDA.B #$53                      ; \
$00:8A8B 8D 09 21     STA.W $2109                     ; / BG3 tilemap at VRAM $5000, 64x64
$00:8A8E A9 00        LDA.B #$00                      ; \
$00:8A90 8D 0B 21     STA.W $210B                     ; / BG1 and BG2 tile data at VRAM $0000
$00:8A93 A9 04        LDA.B #$04                      ; \
$00:8A95 8D 0C 21     STA.W $210C                     ; / BG3 tile data at VRAM $4000, BG4 at $0000
$00:8A98 64 41        STZ $41                         ; [$41] = 0: BG1/BG2 window mask mirror
$00:8A9A 64 42        STZ $42                         ; [$42] = 0: BG3/BG4 window mask mirror
$00:8A9C 64 43        STZ $43                         ; [$43] = 0: OBJ/color window mask mirror
$00:8A9E 9C 2A 21     STZ.W $212A                     ; BG window logic = 0
$00:8AA1 9C 2B 21     STZ.W $212B                     ; OBJ/color window logic = 0
$00:8AA4 9C 2E 21     STZ.W $212E                     ; No window masking on the main screen
$00:8AA7 9C 2F 21     STZ.W $212F                     ; No window masking on the sub screen
$00:8AAA A9 02        LDA.B #$02                      ; \
$00:8AAC 85 44        STA $44                         ; / [$44] = $02: color math mirror (CGWSEL), probably adds the subscreen
$00:8AAE A9 80        LDA.B #$80                      ; \
$00:8AB0 8D 1A 21     STA.W $211A                     ; / M7SEL = $80: Mode 7 area outside the map transparent, no flipping
$00:8AB3 60           RTS                             ; Return



;;; $8AB4..8ACC: Table: sine index adjustments ;;;
;; Used by the Mode 7 matrix routine: indexed by quadrant * 2. The EOR/addend pair turns an in-quadrant offset
;;     into $100 - offset in odd quadrants.
$00:8AB4              .db $00,$00,$FE,$00,$00,$00,$FE,$00 ; Per-quadrant EOR mask for the sine index: $0000, $00FE, $0000, $00FE
$00:8ABC              .db $00,$00,$02,$00,$00,$00,$02,$00 ; Per-quadrant addend: $0000, $0002, $0000, $0002 (with the EOR: $100 - index in odd quadrants)
$00:8AC4              .db $00,$00,$00,$01,$FF,$FF,$00,$10 ; Unreferenced bytes, purpose unclear
$00:8ACC              .db $F0
; |
; V Mode 7 Stuff.. updating M7 mirrors, etc

;;; $8ACD: Calculate Mode 7 rotation matrix ;;;
;; Builds the Mode 7 matrix from the rotation angle [$36] and the scales [$38] and [$39]: A [$2E] = cos *
;;     [$38], B [$30] = sin * [$38],
;; C [$32] = -sin * [$39], D [$34] = cos * [$39]. Values are 8.8 fixed point (a scale of $20 gives $0100).
;;     Called by the Mode 7 boss room code.
;; $008AE8: computes [$30] and [$2E] for scale [$00]. $008B2B: A = (sine table entry X * [$00]) / 32 using the
;;     hardware multiplier.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:985D: Game mode 11: Mario Start, level music (MarioStartGameMode)
;;     $00:987D: Mode 7 boss room: per-frame update
$00:8ACD A5 39        LDA $39                         ; \
$00:8ACF 85 00        STA $00                         ; / [$00] = [$39]: scale for the matrix C and D entries
$00:8AD1 C2 30        REP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 16-bit
$00:8AD3 20 E8 8A     JSR.W $8AE8                     ; [$30] = sin * [$00], [$2E] = cos * [$00]
$00:8AD6 A5 38        LDA $38                         ; \
$00:8AD8 85 00        STA $00                         ; / [$00] = [$38]: scale for the matrix A and B entries
$00:8ADA C2 30        REP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 16-bit
$00:8ADC A5 2E        LDA $2E                         ; \
$00:8ADE 85 34        STA $34                         ; / [$34] (matrix D) = [$2E] = cos * [$39]
$00:8AE0 A5 30        LDA $30                         ; \
$00:8AE2 49 FF FF     EOR.W #$FFFF                    ; |
$00:8AE5 1A           INC A                           ; |
$00:8AE6 85 32        STA $32                         ; / [$32] (matrix C) = -[$30] = -sin * [$39]; then fall into the second pass
$00:8AE8 A5 36        LDA $36                         ; A = [$36]: rotation angle ($0200 = full turn)
$00:8AEA 0A           ASL                             ; A = angle * 2
$00:8AEB 48           PHA                             ; Save angle * 2
$00:8AEC EB           XBA                             ; \
$00:8AED 29 03 00     AND.W #$0003                    ; |
$00:8AF0 0A           ASL                             ; |
$00:8AF1 A8           TAY                             ; / Y = quadrant * 2 (angle bits 7-8)
$00:8AF2 68           PLA                             ; A = angle * 2
$00:8AF3 29 FE 00     AND.W #$00FE                    ; A = (angle & $7F) * 2: byte offset in the quadrant
$00:8AF6 59 B4 8A     EOR.W $8AB4,Y                   ; \
$00:8AF9 18           CLC                             ; |
$00:8AFA 79 BC 8A     ADC.W $8ABC,Y                   ; / A = sine table offset: as is in even quadrants, $100 - offset in odd ones
$00:8AFD AA           TAX                             ; X = sine table offset
$00:8AFE 20 2B 8B     JSR.W $8B2B                     ; A = |sin| * [$00] / 32
$00:8B01 C0 04 00     CPY.W #$0004                    ; \
$00:8B04 90 04        BCC $8B0A                       ; |
$00:8B06 49 FF FF     EOR.W #$FFFF                    ; |
$00:8B09 1A           INC A                           ; / Negate when angle >= $100 (quadrants 2-3): sine is negative there
$00:8B0A 85 30        STA $30                         ; [$30] = sin(angle) * scale (matrix B)
$00:8B0C 8A           TXA                             ; \
$00:8B0D 49 FE 00     EOR.W #$00FE                    ; |
$00:8B10 18           CLC                             ; |
$00:8B11 69 02 00     ADC.W #$0002                    ; |
$00:8B14 29 FF 01     AND.W #$01FF                    ; |
$00:8B17 AA           TAX                             ; / X = $100 - X (wrapped to 9 bits): table offset of the cosine
$00:8B18 20 2B 8B     JSR.W $8B2B                     ; A = |cos| * [$00] / 32
$00:8B1B 88           DEY                             ; \
$00:8B1C 88           DEY                             ; |
$00:8B1D C0 04 00     CPY.W #$0004                    ; |
$00:8B20 B0 04        BCS $8B26                       ; |
$00:8B22 49 FF FF     EOR.W #$FFFF                    ; |
$00:8B25 1A           INC A                           ; / Negate for angles $080-$17F (quadrants 1-2): cosine is negative there
$00:8B26 85 2E        STA $2E                         ; [$2E] = cos(angle) * scale (matrix A)
$00:8B28 E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$00:8B2A 60           RTS                             ; Return

$00:8B2B E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$00:8B2D BD 58 8B     LDA.W $8B58,X                   ; \
$00:8B30 F0 02        BEQ $8B34                       ; |
$00:8B32 A5 00        LDA $00                         ; |
$00:8B34 85 01        STA $01                         ; / [$01] = [$00] if the table entry is $0100, else 0 (high byte of the product)
$00:8B36 BD 57 8B     LDA.W $8B57,X                   ; \
$00:8B39 8D 02 42     STA.W $4202                     ; / Multiplicand = low byte of the table entry
$00:8B3C A5 00        LDA $00                         ; \
$00:8B3E 8D 03 42     STA.W $4203                     ; / Multiplier = scale [$00]; starts the hardware multiply
$00:8B41 EA           NOP                             ; \
$00:8B42 EA           NOP                             ; |
$00:8B43 EA           NOP                             ; |
$00:8B44 EA           NOP                             ; / Wait for the multiplication
$00:8B45 AD 17 42     LDA.W $4217                     ; \
$00:8B48 18           CLC                             ; |
$00:8B49 65 01        ADC $01                         ; |
$00:8B4B EB           XBA                             ; / High byte = product high byte + [$01]
$00:8B4C AD 16 42     LDA.W $4216                     ; Low byte of the product
$00:8B4F C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$00:8B51 4A           LSR                             ; \
$00:8B52 4A           LSR                             ; |
$00:8B53 4A           LSR                             ; |
$00:8B54 4A           LSR                             ; |
$00:8B55 4A           LSR                             ; / A = A / 32 (entry * scale / 32; a scale of $20 gives sin * $100)
$00:8B56 60           RTS                             ; Return



;;; $8B57..8C88: Table: sine values, then unused tilemap words ;;;
;; 129 little-endian words: sin(0..90 degrees) * $100, ending at $0100. The 20 tilemap words after it
;;     ($8C59-$8C80) are not referenced by anything
;; I found. The last 8 bytes are the item box top row used by GM04DoDMA.
$00:8B57              .db $00                         ; Sine table: 129 words, entry n = sin(n * 90/128 degrees) * $100 (low byte first)

$00:8B58              .db $00,$03,$00,$06,$00,$09,$00,$0C
$00:8B60              .db $00,$0F,$00,$12,$00,$15,$00,$19
$00:8B68              .db $00,$1C,$00,$1F,$00,$22,$00,$25
$00:8B70              .db $00,$28,$00,$2B,$00,$2E,$00,$31
$00:8B78              .db $00,$35,$00,$38,$00,$3B,$00,$3E
$00:8B80              .db $00,$41,$00,$44,$00,$47,$00,$4A
$00:8B88              .db $00,$4D,$00,$50,$00,$53,$00,$56
$00:8B90              .db $00,$59,$00,$5C,$00,$5F,$00,$61
$00:8B98              .db $00,$64,$00,$67,$00,$6A,$00,$6D
$00:8BA0              .db $00,$70,$00,$73,$00,$75,$00,$78
$00:8BA8              .db $00,$7B,$00,$7E,$00,$80,$00,$83
$00:8BB0              .db $00,$86,$00,$88,$00,$8B,$00,$8E
$00:8BB8              .db $00,$90,$00,$93,$00,$95,$00,$98
$00:8BC0              .db $00,$9B,$00,$9D,$00,$9F,$00,$A2
$00:8BC8              .db $00,$A4,$00,$A7,$00,$A9,$00,$AB
$00:8BD0              .db $00,$AE,$00,$B0,$00,$B2,$00,$B5
$00:8BD8              .db $00,$B7,$00,$B9,$00,$BB,$00,$BD
$00:8BE0              .db $00,$BF,$00,$C1,$00,$C3,$00,$C5
$00:8BE8              .db $00,$C7,$00,$C9,$00,$CB,$00,$CD
$00:8BF0              .db $00,$CF,$00,$D1,$00,$D3,$00,$D4
$00:8BF8              .db $00,$D6,$00,$D8,$00,$D9,$00,$DB
$00:8C00              .db $00,$DD,$00,$DE,$00,$E0,$00,$E1
$00:8C08              .db $00,$E3,$00,$E4,$00,$E6,$00,$E7
$00:8C10              .db $00,$E8,$00,$EA,$00,$EB,$00,$EC
$00:8C18              .db $00,$ED,$00,$EE,$00,$EF,$00,$F1
$00:8C20              .db $00,$F2,$00,$F3,$00,$F4,$00,$F4
$00:8C28              .db $00,$F5,$00,$F6,$00,$F7,$00,$F8
$00:8C30              .db $00,$F9,$00,$F9,$00,$FA,$00,$FB
$00:8C38              .db $00,$FB,$00,$FC,$00,$FC,$00,$FD
$00:8C40              .db $00,$FD,$00,$FE,$00,$FE,$00,$FE
$00:8C48              .db $00,$FF,$00,$FF,$00,$FF,$00,$FF
$00:8C50              .db $00,$FF,$00,$FF,$00,$FF,$00,$00
$00:8C58              .db $01,$B7,$3C,$B7,$BC,$B8,$3C,$B9 ; High byte of the last entry ($0100 = sin 90 degrees), then 20 unreferenced tilemap words
$00:8C60              .db $3C,$BA,$3C,$BB,$3C,$BA,$3C,$BA
$00:8C68              .db $BC,$BC,$3C,$BD,$3C,$BE,$3C,$BF
$00:8C70              .db $3C,$C0,$3C,$B7,$BC,$C1,$3C,$B9
$00:8C78              .db $3C,$C2,$3C,$C2,$BC,$B7,$3C,$C0
$00:8C80              .db $FC,$3A,$38,$3B,$38,$3B,$38,$3A ; Last byte of those words; then item box top row (4 words, DMA source $8C81)
$00:8C88              .db $78                         ; End of the item box top row (X-flipped corner)


;;; $8C89..8CF9: Table: initial status bar tilemap ;;;
;; Tile/property words for the BG3 status bar: line 1 (28 words), line 2 (27 words) and the item box bottom
;;     row (4 words). Uploaded by GM04DoDMA,
;; which also copies the tile numbers to the RAM mirror at $0EF9.
$00:8C89              .db $30,$28,$31,$28,$32,$28,$33,$28 ; Line 1 (VRAM $5042), words 0-3: tiles $30-$33, probably the MARIO label
$00:8C91              .db $34,$28,$FC,$38,$FC,$3C,$FC,$3C ; Words 4-7: tile $34, then blanks (tile $FC)
$00:8C99              .db $FC,$3C,$FC,$3C,$FC,$38,$FC,$38 ; Words 8-11: blanks
$00:8CA1              .db $4A,$38,$FC,$38,$FC,$38,$4A,$78 ; Words 12-15: item box left border ($4A), 2 blanks, right border ($4A, X-flipped)
$00:8CA9              .db $FC,$38,$3D,$3C,$3E,$3C,$3F,$3C ; Words 16-19: blank, tiles $3D-$3F (probably the TIME label)
$00:8CB1              .db $FC,$38,$FC,$38,$FC,$38,$2E,$3C ; Words 20-23: blanks, tile $2E
$00:8CB9              .db $26,$38,$FC,$38,$FC,$38,$00,$38 ; Words 24-27: tile $26, 2 blanks, digit 0
$00:8CC1              .db $26,$38,$FC,$38,$00,$38,$FC,$38 ; Line 2 (VRAM $5063), words 0-3: tile $26, blank, digit 0, blank
$00:8CC9              .db $FC,$38,$FC,$38,$64,$28,$26,$38 ; Words 4-7: blanks, tile $64, tile $26
$00:8CD1              .db $FC,$38,$FC,$38,$FC,$38,$4A,$38 ; Words 8-11: blanks, item box left border
$00:8CD9              .db $FC,$38,$FC,$38,$4A,$78,$FC,$38 ; Words 12-15: blanks, item box right border, blank
$00:8CE1              .db $FE,$3C,$FE,$3C,$00,$3C,$FC,$38 ; Words 16-19: $FE, $FE, digit 0 (timer digits), blank
$00:8CE9              .db $FC,$38,$FC,$38,$FC,$38,$FC,$38 ; Words 20-23: blanks
$00:8CF1              .db $FC,$38,$FC,$38,$00,$38,$3A,$B8 ; Words 24-26: blank, blank, digit 0; then item box bottom row at $8CF7
$00:8CF9              .db $3B,$B8,$3B,$B8,$3A,$F8     ; End of the item box bottom row (Y-flipped tiles)


;;; $8CFF: Upload initial status bar to VRAM (GM04DoDMA) ;;;
;; Writes the item box top, status bar lines 1 and 2 and the item box bottom into the BG3 tilemap with DMA
;;     channel 1, copies the 55 tile numbers to the
;; mirror at $0EF9 (used by DrawStatusBar) and sets the timer frame countdown [$0F30] = $28.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:985A: Game mode 11: Mario Start, level music (MarioStartGameMode)
;;     $00:A5A8: Game mode 12: prepare level (GM04Load)
$00:8CFF A9 80        LDA.B #$80                      ; \
$00:8D01 8D 15 21     STA.W $2115                     ; / VMAIN = $80: step after high byte writes
$00:8D04 A9 2E        LDA.B #$2E                      ; \
$00:8D06 8D 16 21     STA.W $2116                     ; |
$00:8D09 A9 50        LDA.B #$50                      ; |
$00:8D0B 8D 17 21     STA.W $2117                     ; / VRAM address = $502E (BG3 row 1, column 14: item box top)
$00:8D0E A2 06        LDX.B #$06                      ; \
$00:8D10 BD 90 8D     LDA.W $8D90,X                   ; |
$00:8D13 9D 10 43     STA.W $4310,X                   ; |
$00:8D16 CA           DEX                             ; |
$00:8D17 10 F7        BPL $8D10                       ; / Copy 7 DMA setup bytes to $4310-$4316: $8D90 (source $00:8C81, 8 bytes)
$00:8D19 A9 02        LDA.B #$02                      ; \
$00:8D1B 8D 0B 42     STA.W $420B                     ; / Run DMA channel 1: item box top row
$00:8D1E A9 80        LDA.B #$80                      ; \
$00:8D20 8D 15 21     STA.W $2115                     ; / VMAIN = $80
$00:8D23 A9 42        LDA.B #$42                      ; \
$00:8D25 8D 16 21     STA.W $2116                     ; |
$00:8D28 A9 50        LDA.B #$50                      ; |
$00:8D2A 8D 17 21     STA.W $2117                     ; / VRAM address = $5042 (BG3 row 2, column 2: status bar line 1)
$00:8D2D A2 06        LDX.B #$06                      ; \
$00:8D2F BD 97 8D     LDA.W $8D97,X                   ; |
$00:8D32 9D 10 43     STA.W $4310,X                   ; |
$00:8D35 CA           DEX                             ; |
$00:8D36 10 F7        BPL $8D2F                       ; / Copy 7 DMA setup bytes to $4310-$4316: $8D97 (source $00:8C89, $38 bytes)
$00:8D38 A9 02        LDA.B #$02                      ; \
$00:8D3A 8D 0B 42     STA.W $420B                     ; / Run DMA channel 1: status bar line 1 (28 words)
$00:8D3D A9 80        LDA.B #$80                      ; \
$00:8D3F 8D 15 21     STA.W $2115                     ; / VMAIN = $80
$00:8D42 A9 63        LDA.B #$63                      ; \
$00:8D44 8D 16 21     STA.W $2116                     ; |
$00:8D47 A9 50        LDA.B #$50                      ; |
$00:8D49 8D 17 21     STA.W $2117                     ; / VRAM address = $5063 (BG3 row 3, column 3: status bar line 2)
$00:8D4C A2 06        LDX.B #$06                      ; \
$00:8D4E BD 9E 8D     LDA.W $8D9E,X                   ; |
$00:8D51 9D 10 43     STA.W $4310,X                   ; |
$00:8D54 CA           DEX                             ; |
$00:8D55 10 F7        BPL $8D4E                       ; / Copy 7 DMA setup bytes to $4310-$4316: $8D9E (source $00:8CC1, $36 bytes)
$00:8D57 A9 02        LDA.B #$02                      ; \
$00:8D59 8D 0B 42     STA.W $420B                     ; / Run DMA channel 1: status bar line 2 (27 words)
$00:8D5C A9 80        LDA.B #$80                      ; \
$00:8D5E 8D 15 21     STA.W $2115                     ; / VMAIN = $80
$00:8D61 A9 8E        LDA.B #$8E                      ; \
$00:8D63 8D 16 21     STA.W $2116                     ; |
$00:8D66 A9 50        LDA.B #$50                      ; |
$00:8D68 8D 17 21     STA.W $2117                     ; / VRAM address = $508E (BG3 row 4, column 14: item box bottom)
$00:8D6B A2 06        LDX.B #$06                      ; \
$00:8D6D BD A5 8D     LDA.W $8DA5,X                   ; |
$00:8D70 9D 10 43     STA.W $4310,X                   ; |
$00:8D73 CA           DEX                             ; |
$00:8D74 10 F7        BPL $8D6D                       ; / Copy 7 DMA setup bytes to $4310-$4316: $8DA5 (source $00:8CF7, 8 bytes)
$00:8D76 A9 02        LDA.B #$02                      ; \
$00:8D78 8D 0B 42     STA.W $420B                     ; / Run DMA channel 1: item box bottom row
$00:8D7B A2 36        LDX.B #$36                      ; X = $36: 55 tile numbers to copy
$00:8D7D A0 6C        LDY.B #$6C                      ; Y = $6C: byte offset of the last tilemap word
$00:8D7F B9 89 8C     LDA.W $8C89,Y                   ; Tile number of word Y/2 (the attribute bytes are skipped)
$00:8D82 9D F9 0E     STA.W $0EF9,X                   ; Status bar tile mirror $0EF9+X (line 1 at $0EF9, line 2 at $0F15)
$00:8D85 88           DEY                             ; \
$00:8D86 88           DEY                             ; / Y -= 2
$00:8D87 CA           DEX                             ; X--
$00:8D88 10 F5        BPL $8D7F                       ; Loop for all 55 tiles
$00:8D8A A9 28        LDA.B #$28                      ; \
$00:8D8C 8D 30 0F     STA.W $0F30                     ; / [$0F30] = $28: frame countdown for the level timer
$00:8D8F 60           RTS                             ; Return



;;; $8D90..8DA5: Table: DMA setups for status bar init ;;;
;; Four 7-byte DMA channel 1 setups (DMAP 1, B-bus $18) used by GM04DoDMA.
$00:8D90              .db $01,$18,$81,$8C,$00,$08,$00 ; DMAP 1, B-bus $18, source $00:8C81, $0008 bytes (item box top)

$00:8D97              .db $01,$18,$89,$8C,$00,$38,$00 ; DMAP 1, B-bus $18, source $00:8C89, $0038 bytes (line 1)

$00:8D9E              .db $01,$18,$C1,$8C,$00,$36,$00 ; DMAP 1, B-bus $18, source $00:8CC1, $0036 bytes (line 2)

$00:8DA5              .db $01,$18,$F7,$8C,$00,$08,$00 ; DMAP 1, B-bus $18, source $00:8CF7, $0008 bytes (item box bottom)


;;; $8DAC: Upload status bar tile numbers (DrawStatusBar) ;;;
;; DMAs the tile number mirrors $0EF9 (28 bytes) and $0F15 (27 bytes) to the low bytes of the BG3 tilemap at
;;     $5042 and $5063.
;; Called every NMI. The properties are set once by GM04DoDMA.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:81F4: NMI handler: sound, PPU mirrors, DMA (NMIStart)
;;     $00:82E8: NMI tail: scroll, IRQ setup, Mode 7 path (NMINotSpecialLv)
$00:8DAC 9C 15 21     STZ.W $2115                     ; VMAIN = 0: step after low byte writes (only tile numbers are written)
$00:8DAF A9 42        LDA.B #$42                      ; \
$00:8DB1 8D 16 21     STA.W $2116                     ; |
$00:8DB4 A9 50        LDA.B #$50                      ; |
$00:8DB6 8D 17 21     STA.W $2117                     ; / VRAM address = $5042 (status bar line 1)
$00:8DB9 A2 06        LDX.B #$06                      ; \
$00:8DBB BD E7 8D     LDA.W DMAdata_StBr1,X           ; |
$00:8DBE 9D 10 43     STA.W $4310,X                   ; |
$00:8DC1 CA           DEX                             ; |
$00:8DC2 10 F7        BPL $8DBB                       ; / Copy 7 DMA setup bytes to $4310-$4316: DMAdata_StBr1 (source $00:0EF9, 28 bytes)
$00:8DC4 A9 02        LDA.B #$02                      ; \
$00:8DC6 8D 0B 42     STA.W $420B                     ; / Run DMA channel 1: line 1 tile numbers
$00:8DC9 9C 15 21     STZ.W $2115                     ; VMAIN = 0
$00:8DCC A9 63        LDA.B #$63                      ; \
$00:8DCE 8D 16 21     STA.W $2116                     ; |
$00:8DD1 A9 50        LDA.B #$50                      ; |
$00:8DD3 8D 17 21     STA.W $2117                     ; / VRAM address = $5063 (status bar line 2)
$00:8DD6 A2 06        LDX.B #$06                      ; \
$00:8DD8 BD EE 8D     LDA.W DMAdata_StBr2,X           ; |
$00:8DDB 9D 10 43     STA.W $4310,X                   ; |
$00:8DDE CA           DEX                             ; |
$00:8DDF 10 F7        BPL $8DD8                       ; / Copy 7 DMA setup bytes to $4310-$4316: DMAdata_StBr2 (source $00:0F15, 27 bytes)
$00:8DE1 A9 02        LDA.B #$02                      ; \
$00:8DE3 8D 0B 42     STA.W $420B                     ; / Run DMA channel 1: line 2 tile numbers
$00:8DE6 60           RTS                             ; Return



;;; $8DE7: Table: DMA setup, status bar line 1 (DMAdata_StBr1) ;;;
;; 7 bytes for DrawStatusBar: DMAP 0, B-bus $18, source $00:0EF9, $001C bytes.
$00:8DE7              .db $00,$18,$F9,$0E,$00,$1C,$00 ; DMAP 0, B-bus $18 (VRAM data low), source $00:0EF9, $001C bytes


;;; $8DEE: Status bar: update counters and tiles (DMAdata_StBr2) ;;;
;; Data first: DMA setup for status bar row 2 (source [$0F15], 27 bytes to VRAM), LUIGI name tiles, item box
;;     tile and palette tables, big bonus star digit tiles.
;; Code at $008E1A (called once per frame): runs the level timer (a tick every ~40 frames, hurry-up music at
;;     099, KillMario at 000), clamps scores to 999,999,
;; builds the score, time, coin, lives and bonus star digit tiles in the row buffers [$0EF9] (row 1) and
;;     [$0F15] (row 2), adds pending coins
;; ([$13CC]) one per frame with a 1-up at 100, starts the bonus game at 100 bonus stars, swaps MARIO for LUIGI
;;     and draws the item box and Yoshi coin icons.
;; The tiles are DMAed to VRAM by DrawStatusBar. Tile $FC is the blank tile used to hide leading zeros.
$00:8DEE              .db $00,$18,$15,$0F,$00,$1B,$00 ; DMA setup for status bar row 2: DMAP $00, B-bus $18 (VRAM), source $00:0F15, size $001B

$00:8DF5              .db $40,$41,$42,$43             ; Status bar tiles of the name LUIGI: $40-$44 ($44 is also the first byte of the next row)

$00:8DF9              .db $44,$24,$26,$48,$0E         ; Item box tile by item [$0DC2]: 1 mushroom $24, 2 fire flower $26, 3 star $48, 4 cape $0E

$00:8DFE              .db $00,$02,$04                 ; Item box star palette bits cycle: $00, $02, $04, then $02 (first byte of next table)

$00:8E01              .db $02,$08,$0A,$00,$04         ; Item box palette bits by item: 1 mushroom $08, 2 flower $0A, 3 star (cycles), 4 cape $04

$00:8E06              .db $B7                         ; Big bonus star digit tiles, (top, bottom) per digit 0-9. Digit 0 top = $B7

$00:8E07              .db $C3,$B8,$B9,$BA,$BB,$BA,$BF,$BC ; 0 bottom $C3; 1 = $B8/$B9; 2 = $BA/$BB; 3 = $BA/$BF; 4 top = $BC
$00:8E0F              .db $BD,$BE,$BF,$C0,$C3,$C1,$B9,$C2 ; 4 bottom $BD; 5 = $BE/$BF; 6 = $C0/$C3; 7 = $C1/$B9; 8 top = $C2
$00:8E17              .db $C4,$B7,$C5                 ; 8 bottom $C4; 9 = $B7/$C5

; Yay status bar stuff. Down here, X is commonly used as a "step counter" type thing as well as a index to the tile to handle. Just to put that out there.
$00:8E1A AD 93 14     LDA.W $1493                     ; \
$00:8E1D 05 9D        ORA RAM_SpritesLocked           ; |
$00:8E1F D0 4E        BNE $8E6F                       ; / Level ending ([$1493]) or sprites locked ([$9D]): freeze the timer
$00:8E21 AD 9B 0D     LDA.W $0D9B                     ; \
$00:8E24 C9 C1        CMP.B #$C1                      ; |
$00:8E26 F0 47        BEQ $8E6F                       ; / Bowser fight ([$0D9B] = $C1): the timer does not run
$00:8E28 CE 30 0F     DEC.W $0F30                     ; \
$00:8E2B 10 42        BPL $8E6F                       ; / [$0F30]-- (frames per clock tick); still >= 0: skip the tick
$00:8E2D A9 28        LDA.B #$28                      ; \
$00:8E2F 8D 30 0F     STA.W $0F30                     ; / [$0F30] = $28: next clock tick in about 40 frames
$00:8E32 AD 31 0F     LDA.W $0F31                     ; \
$00:8E35 0D 32 0F     ORA.W $0F32                     ; |
$00:8E38 0D 33 0F     ORA.W $0F33                     ; |
$00:8E3B F0 32        BEQ $8E6F                       ; / Time is already 000: nothing to count down
