;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
;;6-digit HexToDec. Mainly to display the 6-digit (7-digits if you include the rightmost static 0) score counter.
;;Technically, this is 32-bit (using 2 16-bit subtraction for the low word and high word), however, up to 999,999
;;can be displayed correctly.
;;
;;SMW's score is stored internally as a 6-digit number, but is displayed as a 7-digit number with the last digit "0" being static
;;and not being part of this number (123456 would be displayed as "1234560"). To avoid confusion I refer this 6-digit number
;;as "InternalScore"
;;
;;How this works, explained using variables and formulas:
;; n = the digit place value, n=0 is 1s place, n=1 = 10s place, n=2 is the 100s place..., n=5 is the 100,000s place.
;; D[n] = array of digits (also the number of successful subtractions). For example, if InternalScore = $1E240 (123456 in decimal), then:
;;  D[0] = 6 (1s place)
;;  D[1] = 5 (10s place)
;;  D[2] = 4 (...)
;;  D[3] = 3
;;  D[4] = 2
;;  D[5] = 1 (100,000s)
;;SMW converts this  number to BCD like this:
;; 1) Start at the leftmost digit (start with n=5)
;; 2) Set D[n] = 0. Meaning this digit will start at 0.
;; 3) Subtract this  number by [10^n]
;; 4) If the difference do not go below 0, use this difference as the next  minuend, increment D[n] by 1, go to step 3 and continue.
;; 5) If the difference did go below 0, decrement n by 1, and use the same minuend.
;; 6) If n >= 0, go to step 2 and continue.
;;
;;Example: $1E240 (123456)
;;Process digit 5 (subtract by $186A0 (100000) repeatedly):
;;$1E240 (123456, NumbOfSubtracts=0) ->
;; $5BA0 ( 23456, NumbOfSubtracts=1, less than 100000), so digit 5 = 1
;;
;;Process digit 4 (subtract by $2710 (10000) repeatedly):
;; $5BA0 (23456, NumbOfSubtracts=0) ->
;; $3490 (13456, NumbOfSubtracts=1) ->
;;  $D80 ( 3456, NumbOfSubtracts=2, less than 10000), so digit 4 = 2
;;
;;Process digit 3 (subtract by $3E8 (1000) repeatedly):
;; $D80 (3456, NumbOfSubtracts=0) ->
;; $998 (2456, NumbOfSubtracts=1) ->
;; $5B0 (1456, NumbOfSubtracts=2) ->
;; $1C8 ( 456, NumbOfSubtracts=3, less than 1000), so digit 3 = 3
;;
;;Process digit 2 (subtract by $64 (100) repeatedly):
;; $1C8 (456, NumbOfSubtracts=0) ->
;; $164 (356, NumbOfSubtracts=1) ->
;; $100 (256, NumbOfSubtracts=2) ->
;; $9C  (156, NumbOfSubtracts=3) ->
;; $38  ( 56, NumbOfSubtracts=4, less than 100), so digit 2 = 4
;;
;;Process digit 1 (subtract by $A (10) repeatedly):
;; $38 (56, NumbOfSubtracts=0) ->
;; $2E (46, NumbOfSubtracts=1) ->
;; $24 (36, NumbOfSubtracts=2) ->
;; $1A (26, NumbOfSubtracts=3) ->
;; $10 (16, NumbOfSubtracts=4) ->
;  $6  ( 6, NumbOfSubtracts=5, less than 10), so digit 1 = 5
;;
;;Process digit 0 (subtract by $1 (1) repeatedly):
;; $6 (6, NumbOfSubtracts=0) ->
;; $5 (5, NumbOfSubtracts=1) ->
;; $4 (4, NumbOfSubtracts=2) ->
;; $3 (3, NumbOfSubtracts=3) ->
;; $2 (2, NumbOfSubtracts=4) ->
;; $1 (1, NumbOfSubtracts=5) ->
;; $0 (0, NumbOfSubtracts=6, less than 1), so digit 0 = 6
;;
;;In summary, this is the "left-to-right" version of this: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Positional_notation#Base_conversion
;;Which in that link, you divide by 10 (using euclidean division; Q and R) repeatedly and each time, the remainder is the
;;digit of the result (starting at the ones place), while the quotient is the next dividend to be divided by 10 and repeats.
;;
;; Using the same example above via the right-to-left method:
;; $1E240/10 = Q: $3039, R: 6 (1s)
;; $3039/10  = Q: $4D2,  R: 5 (10s)
;; $4D2/10   = Q: $7B,   R: 4 (100s)
;; $7B/10    = Q: $C     R: 3 (1,000s)
;; $C/10     = Q: $1     R: 2 (10,000s)
;; $1/10     = Q: $0     R: 1 (100,000s)
;; ...
;;
;;This method handles the 100,000s place first, and works its towards the 1s place. Instead of dividing by 10^n where n
;;increases (you divided by 10 repeatedly, which is x/(10^n)), you divide by 10^n as n decreases. SMW (nor the SNES) does not have a
;;32-bit division routine/register, so repeated subtraction is used to emulate the euclidean division (Q = number of successful
;;subtraction, R: Number to be subtracted by lower powers of ten). Each remainder in the loop after it cannot subtract is then
;;reused to subtract by 10^(n-1), therefore this entire hexdec is one big long division.
;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;

;;; $8FFA..8FFC: Table: powers of ten for decimal conversion ;;;
;; Six 32-bit entries (high word, low word): 100,000, 10,000, 1,000, 100, 10, 1. Used with Y = 4 * entry by
;;     the routines at $009012 and $009051.
$00:8FFA              dw $0001                        ; Powers of ten, 32-bit: 100,000 high word $0001 (entries are 4 bytes: high, low)
$00:8FFC              dw $86A0                        ; 100,000 low word $86A0 (followed by 10,000, 1,000, 100, 10 and 1)
; dw $0000 ;>10,000s (high word)  ;>Index_008FFA = $04 Index_008FFC = $02
; dw $2710 ;>10,000s (low word)   ;>Index_008FFA = $06 Index_008FFC = $04
; dw $0000 ;>1,000s (high word)   ;>Index_008FFA = $08 Index_008FFC = $06
; dw $03E8 ;>1,000s (low word)    ;>Index_008FFA = $0A Index_008FFC = $08
; dw $0000 ;>100s (high word)     ;>Index_008FFA = $0C Index_008FFC = $0A
; dw $0064 ;>100s (low word)      ;>Index_008FFA = $0E Index_008FFC = $0C
; dw $0000 ;>10s (high word)      ;>Index_008FFA = $10 Index_008FFC = $0E
; dw $000A ;>10s (low word)       ;>Index_008FFA = $12 Index_008FFC = $10
; dw $0000 ;>1s (high word)       ;>Index_008FFA = $14 Index_008FFC = $12
; dw $0001 ;>1s (low word)        ;>Index_008FFA = $16 Index_008FFC = $14
;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
;;Here:
;;*$00-$01: High word (word = 2 bytes; 16-bit) of subtrahend that shouldn't underflow
;;*$02-$03: Low word of subtrahend that shouldn't underflow
;;*$04-$05: High word of subtrahend that can underflow (use as a preview if the next subtraction underflows)
;;*$06-$07: Low word of subtrahend that can underflow (use as a preview if the next subtraction underflows)
;;*STZ.W $0F15,X is D[n] = 0 before each digit processing
;;*INC.W $0F15 is D[n] being incremented of how many times you can subtract without going in the negatives.
;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;

;;; $9012: Convert 32-bit value to six decimal digit tiles ;;;
;; Counts how many times each power of ten can be subtracted from the 32-bit value, one tile per digit (left
;;     to right).
;; Parameters: [$00]-[$01] high word, [$02]-[$03] low word of the value; X = offset into the tile buffer
;;     [$0F15]; Y = 0 (start at 100,000s).
;; Returns: digit tiles at [$0F15+X]...; the value variables are destroyed.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:8EDB: Status bar: update counters and tiles (DMAdata_StBr2)
;;     $00:8F09: Status bar: update counters and tiles (DMAdata_StBr2)
$00:9012 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$00:9014 9E 15 0F     STZ.W $0F15,X                   ; Digit tile [$0F15+X] = 0
$00:9017 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$00:9019 A5 02        LDA $02                         ; \
$00:901B 38           SEC                             ; |
$00:901C F9 FC 8F     SBC.W $8FFC,Y                   ; |
$00:901F 85 06        STA $06                         ; / [$06] = [$02] - low word of 10^n (SBC $8FFC,Y)
$00:9021 A5 00        LDA $00                         ; \
$00:9023 F9 FA 8F     SBC.W $8FFA,Y                   ; |
$00:9026 85 04        STA $04                         ; / [$04] = [$00] - high word of 10^n - borrow (SBC $8FFA,Y)
$00:9028 90 0F        BCC $9039                       ; Borrow (value < 10^n): this digit is finished
$00:902A A5 06        LDA $06                         ; \
$00:902C 85 02        STA $02                         ; |
$00:902E A5 04        LDA $04                         ; |
$00:9030 85 00        STA $00                         ; / Value = difference
$00:9032 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$00:9034 FE 15 0F     INC.W $0F15,X                   ; Digit tile [$0F15+X]++ (counts the successful subtractions)
$00:9037 80 DE        BRA $9017                       ; Subtract again

$00:9039 E8           INX                             ; Next digit tile: X++
$00:903A C8           INY                             ; \
$00:903B C8           INY                             ; |
$00:903C C8           INY                             ; |
$00:903D C8           INY                             ; / Y += 4: next power of ten
$00:903E C0 18        CPY.B #$18                      ; \
$00:9040 D0 D0        BNE $9012                       ; / Y = $18 (past the ones place)? No: next digit
$00:9042 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$00:9044 60           RTS                             ; Return

;This is the 8-bit Hex->Dec, ideal for 2-digit counters.
;you could make this 3-digits by calling this routine again
;after writing the 1s and 10s by taking the X, TXA it, then
;call this, and then A should now be the hundreds digit (0-2)
;with Y always 0 (up to 0255).

;;; $9045: Hex to decimal and item box drawing (HexToDec) ;;;
;; $009045: converts A (0-99) to decimal by repeated subtraction. Returns: X = tens, A = ones.
;; $009051: 16-bit version of the routine above, used for the bonus star counter. Parameters: [$02] value, X =
;;     tile offset ([$0F15+X]), Y = 4 * first power of ten (Y = $10 gives two digits).
;; $009079: draws the item box sprite (reserve item [$0DC2]) at X = $78, Y = $0F as a 16x16 sprite; the star
;;     flashes through palettes. Hides OAM slot 0 in Mode 7 boss rooms.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:8F4D: Status bar: update counters and tiles (DMAdata_StBr2)
;;     $00:8F76: Status bar: update counters and tiles (DMAdata_StBr2)
;;     $00:974C: Game mode 11: Mario Start, level music (MarioStartGameMode)
;;     $00:9D76: Game mode 08: file select, mode 0A: players
$00:9045 A2 00        LDX.B #$00                      ; X = 0: tens counter
$00:9047 C9 0A        CMP.B #$0A                      ; \
$00:9049 90 05        BCC $9050                       ; / A < 10: done, A = ones digit
$00:904B E9 0A        SBC.B #$0A                      ; \
$00:904D E8           INX                             ; |
$00:904E 80 F7        BRA $9047                       ; / A -= 10; X++; repeat
$00:9050 60           RTS                             ; Return: A = ones, X = tens

;Bonus stars Hex->Dec. I do not know why Nintendo decided to use this
;same Hex->Dec as the score since bonus stars are never to display 3-digits.
;Routine starts with Y=$10, X=$09.
$00:9051 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$00:9053 9E 15 0F     STZ.W $0F15,X                   ; Digit tile [$0F15+X] = 0
$00:9056 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$00:9058 A5 02        LDA $02                         ; \
$00:905A 38           SEC                             ; |
$00:905B F9 FC 8F     SBC.W $8FFC,Y                   ; |
$00:905E 85 06        STA $06                         ; / [$06] = [$02] - low word of 10^n
$00:9060 90 0B        BCC $906D                       ; Borrow: this digit is finished
$00:9062 A5 06        LDA $06                         ; \
$00:9064 85 02        STA $02                         ; / Value = difference
$00:9066 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$00:9068 FE 15 0F     INC.W $0F15,X                   ; Digit tile [$0F15+X]++
$00:906B 80 E9        BRA $9056                       ; Subtract again

$00:906D E8           INX                             ; Next digit tile: X++
$00:906E C8           INY                             ; \
$00:906F C8           INY                             ; |
$00:9070 C8           INY                             ; |
$00:9071 C8           INY                             ; / Y += 4: next power of ten
$00:9072 C0 18        CPY.B #$18                      ; \
$00:9074 D0 DB        BNE $9051                       ; / Until Y = $18 (past the ones place)
$00:9076 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$00:9078 60           RTS                             ; Return

$00:9079 A0 E0        LDY.B #$E0                      ; Y = $E0: OAM offset of the item box sprite
$00:907B 2C 9B 0D     BIT.W $0D9B                     ; V = [$0D9B] bit 6 (Mode 7 boss room)
$00:907E 50 0E        BVC $908E                       ; Not a boss room: keep Y = $E0
$00:9080 A0 00        LDY.B #$00                      ; Boss room: use OAM slot 0
$00:9082 AD 9B 0D     LDA.W $0D9B                     ; \
$00:9085 C9 C1        CMP.B #$C1                      ; |
$00:9087 F0 05        BEQ $908E                       ; / Bowser ([$0D9B] = $C1): leave slot 0 alone
$00:9089 A9 F0        LDA.B #$F0                      ; \
$00:908B 99 01 02     STA.W OAM_ExtendedDispY,Y       ; / Hide the sprite in slot 0 (Y = $F0), it is only shown when the box holds an item
$00:908E 84 01        STY $01                         ; [$01] = OAM offset of the item box sprite
$00:9090 AC C2 0D     LDY.W $0DC2                     ; \
$00:9093 F0 3B        BEQ $90D0                       ; / Y = item box item [$0DC2]; 0 = empty: return
$00:9095 B9 01 8E     LDA.W $8E01,Y                   ; \
$00:9098 85 00        STA $00                         ; / [$00] = palette bits for this item ($8E01)
$00:909A C0 03        CPY.B #$03                      ; \
$00:909C D0 0D        BNE $90AB                       ; / Not the star: keep it
$00:909E A5 13        LDA RAM_FrameCounter            ; \
$00:90A0 4A           LSR                             ; |
$00:90A1 29 03        AND.B #$03                      ; |
$00:90A3 5A           PHY                             ; |
$00:90A4 A8           TAY                             ; |
$00:90A5 B9 FE 8D     LDA.W $8DFE,Y                   ; |
$00:90A8 7A           PLY                             ; |
$00:90A9 85 00        STA $00                         ; / Star: palette bits cycle through $8DFE every 2 frames ([$13] >> 1 AND 3)
$00:90AB A4 01        LDY $01                         ; Y = OAM offset
$00:90AD A9 78        LDA.B #$78                      ; \
$00:90AF 99 00 02     STA.W OAM_ExtendedDispX,Y       ; / Sprite X = $78
$00:90B2 A9 0F        LDA.B #$0F                      ; \
$00:90B4 99 01 02     STA.W OAM_ExtendedDispY,Y       ; / Sprite Y = $0F
$00:90B7 A9 30        LDA.B #$30                      ; \
$00:90B9 05 00        ORA $00                         ; |
$00:90BB 99 03 02     STA.W OAM_ExtendedProp,Y        ; / Properties = $30 (priority 3) | palette bits [$00]
$00:90BE AE C2 0D     LDX.W $0DC2                     ; \
$00:90C1 BD F9 8D     LDA.W $8DF9,X                   ; |
$00:90C4 99 02 02     STA.W OAM_ExtendedTile,Y        ; / Tile = $8DF9[item]
$00:90C7 98           TYA                             ; \
$00:90C8 4A           LSR                             ; |
$00:90C9 4A           LSR                             ; |
$00:90CA A8           TAY                             ; |
$00:90CB A9 02        LDA.B #$02                      ; |
$00:90CD 99 20 04     STA.W $0420,Y                   ; / OAM size table [$0420 + OAM offset / 4] = 2: 16x16 sprite, X bit 8 clear
$00:90D0 60           RTS                             ; Return



;;; $90D1..9101: Table: text sprite tiles, upper half ;;;
;; Indexed by text column ($91E9). Probably the letters of the Mario Start! / bonus game messages; $FF =
;;     blank column.
$00:90D1              .db $00,$FF,$4D,$4C,$03,$4D,$5D,$FF ; Tile numbers of the upper sprite of each text column; $FF = blank column
$00:90D9              .db $03,$00,$4C,$03,$04,$15,$00,$02
$00:90E1              .db $00,$4A,$4E,$FF,$4C,$4B,$4A,$03
$00:90E9              .db $5F,$05,$04,$03,$02,$00,$FF,$01
$00:90F1              .db $4A,$5F,$05,$04,$00,$4D,$5D,$03
$00:90F9              .db $02,$01,$00,$FF,$5B,$14,$5F,$01
$00:9101              .db $5E,$FF,$FF,$FF


;;; $9105..9135: Table: text sprite tiles, lower half ;;;
;; Same indexes as $90D1; tile of the sprite drawn 8 pixels below the upper one.
$00:9105              .db $10,$FF,$00,$5C,$13,$00,$5D,$FF ; Tile numbers of the lower sprite of each text column
$00:910D              .db $03,$00,$5C,$13,$14,$15,$00,$12
$00:9115              .db $00,$03,$5E,$FF,$5C,$4B,$5A,$03
$00:911D              .db $5F,$05,$14,$13,$12,$10,$FF,$11
$00:9125              .db $03,$5F,$05,$14,$00,$00,$5D,$03
$00:912D              .db $12,$11,$10,$FF,$5B,$01,$5F,$01
$00:9135              .db $5E,$FF,$FF,$FF


;;; $9139..9169: Table: text sprite properties, upper half ;;;
$00:9139              .db $34,$00,$34,$34,$34,$34,$30,$00 ; Properties of the upper sprite of each text column
$00:9141              .db $34,$34,$34,$34,$74,$34,$34,$34
$00:9149              .db $34,$34,$34,$00,$34,$34,$34,$34
$00:9151              .db $34,$34,$34,$34,$34,$34,$00,$34
$00:9159              .db $34,$34,$34,$34,$34,$34,$34,$34
$00:9161              .db $34,$34,$34,$34,$34,$34,$34,$34
$00:9169              .db $34


;;; $916A..919A: Table: text sprite properties, lower half ;;;
;; Mostly the upper values with the Y flip bit set, so the lower sprite looks like a mirrored copy of the
;;     upper one (probably a reflection).
$00:916A              .db $34,$00,$B4,$34,$34,$B4,$F0,$00 ; Properties of the lower sprite of each text column (Y flip set in most)
$00:9172              .db $B4,$B4,$34,$34,$74,$B4,$B4,$34
$00:917A              .db $B4,$B4,$34,$00,$34,$B4,$34,$B4
$00:9182              .db $B4,$B4,$34,$34,$34,$34,$00,$34
$00:918A              .db $B4,$B4,$B4,$34,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4
$00:9192              .db $34,$34,$34,$34,$F4,$B4,$F4,$B4
$00:919A              .db $B4


;;; $919B: Mario Start text and level setup helpers ;;;
;; $00919B: during Mario animation $0A runs the Mario animation handler; otherwise sets [$0DC0] = $1E when
;;     [$141A] is 0 (purpose unclear).
;; $0091B1: draws the "Mario Start!" / "Luigi Start!" text (or the bonus game text when [$1425] is set, which
;;     also zeroes the timer) as 14 columns of two sprites.
;; $0091E9: draws one text column from the tables at $0090D1-$00916A at X position [$00] and steps [$00] left
;;     by 8.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:A5F0: Game mode 12: prepare level (GM04Load)
$00:919B A5 71        LDA RAM_MarioAnimation          ; \
$00:919D C9 0A        CMP.B #$0A                      ; |
$00:919F D0 05        BNE $91A6                       ; / Mario animation [$71] != $0A: continue below
$00:91A1 20 93 C5     JSR.W $C593                     ; Run the Mario animation routine for [$71] ($C593)
$00:91A4 80 0A        BRA $91B0                       ; Return

$00:91A6 AD 1A 14     LDA.W $141A                     ; \
$00:91A9 D0 05        BNE $91B0                       ; / [$141A] != 0: return
$00:91AB A9 1E        LDA.B #$1E                      ; \
$00:91AD 8D C0 0D     STA.W $0DC0                     ; / [$0DC0] = $1E (purpose unclear)
$00:91B0 60           RTS                             ; Return

$00:91B1 20 2D A8     JSR.W $A82D                     ; Prepare the text graphics in RAM ($A82D), probably the Mario Start! font
$00:91B4 A2 00        LDX.B #$00                      ; X = 0: index of the first text column
$00:91B6 A9 B0        LDA.B #$B0                      ; A = $B0: X position of the first (rightmost) column
$00:91B8 AC 25 14     LDY.W $1425                     ; \
$00:91BB F0 0D        BEQ $91CA                       ; / [$1425] = 0: normal text, skip the bonus game setup
$00:91BD 9C 31 0F     STZ.W $0F31                     ; \
$00:91C0 9C 32 0F     STZ.W $0F32                     ; |
$00:91C3 9C 33 0F     STZ.W $0F33                     ; / Bonus game: time = 000
$00:91C6 A2 26        LDX.B #$26                      ; X = $26: start index of the bonus game text
$00:91C8 A9 A4        LDA.B #$A4                      ; A = $A4: X position of its first column
$00:91CA 85 00        STA $00                         ; \
$00:91CC 64 01        STZ $01                         ; / [$00]-[$01] = X position of the current column (16-bit)
$00:91CE A0 70        LDY.B #$70                      ; Y = $70: OAM offset of the first column (counts down by 8)
$00:91D0 20 E9 91     JSR.W $91E9                     ; Draw one text column (two sprites) ($91E9)
$00:91D3 E8           INX                             ; Next column index: X++
$00:91D4 E0 08        CPX.B #$08                      ; \
$00:91D6 D0 07        BNE $91DF                       ; / X != 8: keep going
$00:91D8 AD B3 0D     LDA.W $0DB3                     ; \
$00:91DB F0 02        BEQ $91DF                       ; / Mario ([$0DB3] = 0): continue with the same indexes
$00:91DD A2 0E        LDX.B #$0E                      ; Luigi: jump to index $0E, which probably holds the LUIGI letters
$00:91DF 98           TYA                             ; \
$00:91E0 38           SEC                             ; |
$00:91E1 E9 08        SBC.B #$08                      ; |
$00:91E3 A8           TAY                             ; / Y -= 8: OAM offset of the next column
$00:91E4 D0 EA        BNE $91D0                       ; Loop for all 14 columns
$00:91E6 4C 94 84     JMP.W $8494                     ; Pack the OAM size bits and return ($8494)

$00:91E9 BD 39 91     LDA.W $9139,X                   ; \
$00:91EC 99 0B 03     STA.W OAM_Tile3Prop,Y           ; / Upper sprite properties = $9139[X]
$00:91EF BD 6A 91     LDA.W $916A,X                   ; \
$00:91F2 99 0F 03     STA.W OAM_Tile4Prop,Y           ; / Lower sprite properties = $916A[X]
$00:91F5 A5 00        LDA $00                         ; \
$00:91F7 99 08 03     STA.W OAM_Tile3DispX,Y          ; |
$00:91FA 99 0C 03     STA.W OAM_Tile4DispX,Y          ; / X position of both sprites = [$00]
$00:91FD 38           SEC                             ; \
$00:91FE E9 08        SBC.B #$08                      ; |
$00:9200 85 00        STA $00                         ; |
$00:9202 B0 02        BCS $9206                       ; |
$00:9204 C6 01        DEC $01                         ; / [$00]-[$01] -= 8 (16-bit): next column is 8 pixels to the left
$00:9206 5A           PHY                             ; Save Y
$00:9207 98           TYA                             ; \
$00:9208 4A           LSR                             ; |
$00:9209 4A           LSR                             ; |
$00:920A A8           TAY                             ; / Y = OAM offset / 4
$00:920B A5 01        LDA $01                         ; \
$00:920D 29 01        AND.B #$01                      ; |
$00:920F 99 62 04     STA.W $0462,Y                   ; |
$00:9212 99 63 04     STA.W $0463,Y                   ; / X bit 8 ([$01] bit 0) into the OAM size table for both sprites ($0462 and $0463 + Y)
$00:9215 7A           PLY                             ; Restore Y
$00:9216 BD D1 90     LDA.W $90D1,X                   ; \
$00:9219 30 13        BMI $922E                       ; / Upper tile = $90D1[X]; bit 7 set = blank column, return
$00:921B 99 0A 03     STA.W OAM_Tile3,Y               ; Upper sprite tile
$00:921E BD 05 91     LDA.W $9105,X                   ; \
$00:9221 99 0E 03     STA.W OAM_Tile4,Y               ; / Lower sprite tile = $9105[X]
$00:9224 A9 68        LDA.B #$68                      ; \
$00:9226 99 09 03     STA.W OAM_Tile3DispY,Y          ; / Upper sprite Y = $68
$00:9229 A9 70        LDA.B #$70                      ; \
$00:922B 99 0D 03     STA.W OAM_Tile4DispY,Y          ; / Lower sprite Y = $70
$00:922E 60           RTS                             ; Return

; V This code is kinda finishing and finalizing showing the Nitendo Presents.  V

;;; $922F: Set CGRAM color 0 to black by DMA (NintenDMAINIT) ;;;
;; Clears the palette mirror word [$0703] and DMAs it into CGRAM color 0 with channel 2. Used at the Nintendo
;;     Presents screen and the ending.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:93E0: Game mode 00: load Nintendo Presents (NintendoTile)
;;     $00:94DD: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:9612: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:9675: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:9AA1: Detect connected controllers into [$0DA0] (SetUp0DA0GM4)
;;     $00:A150: Game mode 0C: load overworld (LoadMapGameMode)
;;     $00:A5CF: Game mode 12: prepare level (GM04Load)
$00:922F 9C 03 07     STZ.W $0703                     ; \
$00:9232 9C 04 07     STZ.W $0704                     ; / Palette mirror word [$0703] = $0000 (black)
$00:9235 9C 21 21     STZ.W $2121                     ; CGRAM address = 0
$00:9238 A2 06        LDX.B #$06                      ; X = 6: seven bytes of DMA setup
$00:923A BD 49 92     LDA.W $9249,X                   ; \
$00:923D 9D 20 43     STA.W $4320,X                   ; |
$00:9240 CA           DEX                             ; |
$00:9241 10 F7        BPL $923A                       ; / Copy $9249 to DMA channel 2 registers $4320-$4326
$00:9243 A9 04        LDA.B #$04                      ; \
$00:9245 8D 0B 42     STA.W $420B                     ; / Start DMA channel 2: copy [$0703] to CGRAM color 0
$00:9248 60           RTS                             ; Return



;;; $9249..9249: Table: DMA setup for black backdrop ;;;
$00:9249              .db $00,$22,$03,$07,$00,$00,$02 ; DMAP $00, B-bus $22 (CGDATA), source $00:0703, size $0002


;;; $9250: Init HDMA window effect (channel 7) ;;;
;; Sets up HDMA channel 7 to write the window registers WH0/WH1 from an indirect table, disables all HDMA
;;     ([$0D9F] = 0) and fills the window table
;; at $04A0-$065F (224 lines of left, right) with left = $FF, right = $00 so no screen area is inside the
;;     window.
;; $009260 is the entry used to just disable HDMA, $009263 clears the table only.
$00:9250 A2 04        LDX.B #$04                      ; X = 4: five bytes of HDMA channel 7 setup
$00:9252 BD 77 92     LDA.W $9277,X                   ; \
$00:9255 9D 70 43     STA.W $4370,X                   ; |
$00:9258 CA           DEX                             ; |
$00:9259 10 F7        BPL $9252                       ; / Copy $9277 to $4370-$4374: indirect window table at $00:927C
$00:925B A9 00        LDA.B #$00                      ; \
$00:925D 8D 77 43     STA.W $4377                     ; / HDMA channel 7 indirect bank $4377 = $00
$00:9260 9C 9F 0D     STZ.W $0D9F                     ; Disable all HDMA channels ([$0D9F] = 0)
$00:9263 C2 10        REP #$10                        ; Index 16-bit
$00:9265 A2 BE 01     LDX.W #$01BE                    ; X = $01BE: offset of the last of 224 line entries
$00:9268 A9 FF        LDA.B #$FF                      ; A = $FF
$00:926A 9D A0 04     STA.W $04A0,X                   ; \
$00:926D 9E A1 04     STZ.W $04A1,X                   ; |
$00:9270 CA           DEX                             ; |
$00:9271 CA           DEX                             ; |
$00:9272 10 F6        BPL $926A                       ; / Window table at $04A0-$065F: every line left = $FF, right = $00 (empty window)
$00:9274 E2 10        SEP #$10                        ; \
$00:9276 60           RTS                             ; / Index 8-bit and return



;;; $9277..927F: HDMA setup and table: window effect ;;;
$00:9277              .db $41,$26,$7C,$92,$00,$F0,$A0,$04 ; HDMA channel 7: DMAP $41 (indirect, two registers), B-bus $26 (WH0/WH1), table $00:927C
$00:927F              .db $F0,$80,$05,$00             ; Table end: $F0 = 112 lines from $0580, then $00 (the entry at $00927C is $F0 = 112 lines from $04A0)


;;; $9283: Window HDMA: enable fully covered window ;;;
;; Clears the window table, then (unless [$0D9B] bit 0 is set) fills the last line with a window covering the
;;     whole line and enables channel 7.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:9A1C: Boss room tile animation and Mode 7 setup
$00:9283 20 63 92     JSR.W $9263                     ; Clear the window table ($9263)
$00:9286 AD 9B 0D     LDA.W $0D9B                     ; \
$00:9289 4A           LSR                             ; |
$00:928A B0 14        BCS $92A0                       ; / [$0D9B] bit 0 set: skip opening the window, just enable HDMA ($0092A0)
$00:928C C2 10        REP #$10                        ; Index 16-bit
$00:928E A2 BE 01     LDX.W #$01BE                    ; X = $01BE: last line entry

;;; $9291: Fill window table lines, set up scroll HDMA (WindowHDMAenable) ;;;
;; $009291: loop that writes left = $00, right = $FF entries from offset X upwards to the end of the window
;;     table, then enables HDMA channel 7 ([$0D9F] = $80).
;; $0092A8: clears the table and opens the last 20 lines through the loop above.
;; $0092B2: used in the ending (game mode $23). Sets up HDMA channels 5-7 to write BG1, BG2 and BG3 horizontal
;;     scroll per scanline from tables at $04A0, $04AA, $04B4
;; (10 bytes each: 88-line segments with the scroll words taken from [$1A], [$1E], [$22] and [$1462]...);
;;     enables channels 5-7 ([$0D9F] = $E0).
$00:9291 9E A0 04     STZ.W $04A0,X                   ; Left edge of this line = $00
$00:9294 A9 FF        LDA.B #$FF                      ; \
$00:9296 9D A1 04     STA.W $04A1,X                   ; / Right edge = $FF: the line is fully covered by the window
$00:9299 E8           INX                             ; \
$00:929A E8           INX                             ; / X += 2: next line
$00:929B E0 C0 01     CPX.W #$01C0                    ; \
$00:929E 90 F1        BCC WindowHDMAenable            ; / Loop until X >= $01C0
$00:92A0 A9 80        LDA.B #$80                      ; \
$00:92A2 8D 9F 0D     STA.W $0D9F                     ; / Enable HDMA channel 7 only ([$0D9F] = $80)
$00:92A5 E2 10        SEP #$10                        ; Index 8-bit
$00:92A7 60           RTS                             ; Return

$00:92A8 20 63 92     JSR.W $9263                     ; Clear the window table ($9263)
$00:92AB C2 10        REP #$10                        ; Index 16-bit
$00:92AD A2 98 01     LDX.W #$0198                    ; X = $0198: line 204, so the last 20 lines are opened
$00:92B0 80 DF        BRA WindowHDMAenable            ; Fill them with the fully covered window above

$00:92B2 A9 58        LDA.B #$58                      ; A = $58: line count (88 lines) of the first segment of each table
$00:92B4 8D A0 04     STA.W $04A0                     ; \
$00:92B7 8D AA 04     STA.W $04AA                     ; |
$00:92BA 8D B4 04     STA.W $04B4                     ; / First byte of the tables at $04A0, $04AA and $04B4 = $58
$00:92BD 9C A9 04     STZ.W $04A9                     ; \
$00:92C0 9C B3 04     STZ.W $04B3                     ; |
$00:92C3 9C BD 04     STZ.W $04BD                     ; / Last byte of each 10-byte table = 0 (end of HDMA table)
$00:92C6 A2 04        LDX.B #$04                      ; X = 4: five setup bytes per channel
$00:92C8 BD 13 93     LDA.W $9313,X                   ; \
$00:92CB 9D 50 43     STA.W $4350,X                   ; / Channel 5 setup byte X from $9313
$00:92CE BD 18 93     LDA.W $9318,X                   ; \
$00:92D1 9D 60 43     STA.W $4360,X                   ; / Channel 6 setup byte X from $9318
$00:92D4 BD 1D 93     LDA.W $931D,X                   ; \
$00:92D7 9D 70 43     STA.W $4370,X                   ; / Channel 7 setup byte X from $931D
$00:92DA CA           DEX                             ; X--
$00:92DB 10 EB        BPL $92C8                       ; Loop for all five bytes
$00:92DD A9 00        LDA.B #$00                      ; \
$00:92DF 8D 57 43     STA.W $4357                     ; |
$00:92E2 8D 67 43     STA.W $4367                     ; |
$00:92E5 8D 77 43     STA.W $4377                     ; / Indirect banks of channels 5-7 ($4357, $4367, $4377) = $00 (unused in direct mode)
$00:92E8 A9 E0        LDA.B #$E0                      ; \
$00:92EA 8D 9F 0D     STA.W $0D9F                     ; / Enable HDMA channels 5, 6 and 7 ([$0D9F] = $E0)
$00:92ED C2 30        REP #$30                        ; A and index 16-bit
$00:92EF A0 08 00     LDY.W #$0008                    ; Y = 8: offset of BG3's scroll ([$1A] + 8 = [$22])
$00:92F2 A2 14 00     LDX.W #$0014                    ; X = $14: offset of the BG3 table ($04B4 - $04A0)
$00:92F5 B9 1A 00     LDA.W RAM_ScreenBndryXLo,Y      ; \
$00:92F8 9D A1 04     STA.W $04A1,X                   ; |
$00:92FB 9D A4 04     STA.W $04A4,X                   ; / Segments 1 and 2 scroll = [$1A+Y] (BG1 [$1A], BG2 [$1E], BG3 [$22] horizontal scroll)
$00:92FE B9 62 14     LDA.W $1462,Y                   ; \
$00:9301 9D A7 04     STA.W $04A7,X                   ; / Segment 3 scroll = [$1462+Y]
$00:9304 8A           TXA                             ; \
$00:9305 38           SEC                             ; |
$00:9306 E9 0A 00     SBC.W #$000A                    ; |
$00:9309 AA           TAX                             ; / X -= $0A: previous 10-byte table
$00:930A 88           DEY                             ; \
$00:930B 88           DEY                             ; |
$00:930C 88           DEY                             ; |
$00:930D 88           DEY                             ; / Y -= 4: previous layer
$00:930E 10 E5        BPL $92F5                       ; Loop for the three layers
$00:9310 E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A and index 8-bit
$00:9312 60           RTS                             ; Return



;;; $9313..931D: Table: HDMA setup for BG scroll channels ;;;
;; Five bytes per channel (DMAP, B-bus, table address low and high, bank) for channels 5, 6 and 7.
$00:9313              .db $02,$0D,$A0,$04,$00         ; HDMA channel 5: DMAP $02, B-bus $0D (BG1HOFS), table $00:04A0

$00:9318              .db $02,$0F,$AA,$04,$00         ; HDMA channel 6: DMAP $02, B-bus $0F (BG2HOFS), table $00:04AA

$00:931D              .db $02,$11,$B4,$04,$00         ; HDMA channel 7: DMAP $02, B-bus $11 (BG3HOFS), table $00:04B4


;;; $9322: Run current game mode (GetGameMode) ;;;
;; Jumps to the routine for the game mode in [$0100] using the pointer table that follows the JSL
;;     (ExecutePtr).
$00:9322 AD 00 01     LDA.W RAM_GameMode              ; A = game mode [$0100]
$00:9325 22 DF 86 00  JSL.L ExecutePtr                ; Run the routine from the pointer table below (ExecutePtr)


;;; $9329: Pointer table: game modes (Ptrs009329) ;;;
;; One 16-bit pointer per game mode ($00-$29), indexed by [$0100]. Names inferred from the code; several are
;;     marked as uncertain.
$00:9329 91 93        .dw $9391                       ; 00 - Load Nintendo Presents
$00:932B 0F 94        .dw $940F                       ; 01 - Nintendo Presents screen
$00:932D 6F 9F        .dw $9F6F                       ; 02 - Fade to title screen
$00:932F AE 96        .dw $96AE                       ; 03 - Load title screen
$00:9331 8B 9A        .dw $9A8B                       ; 04 - Prepare title screen
$00:9333 6F 9F        .dw $9F6F                       ; 05 - Title screen: fade in
$00:9335 1B 94        .dw $941B                       ; 06 - Title screen: circle effect
$00:9337 64 9C        .dw GAMEMODE_07                 ; 07 - Title screen
$00:9339 D1 9C        .dw $9CD1                       ; 08 - File select screen
$00:933B 1A 9B        .dw $9B1A                       ; 09 - File erase screen
$00:933D FA 9D        .dw $9DFA                       ; 0A - Player select screen
$00:933F 6F 9F        .dw $9F6F                       ; 0B - Fade out of title screen or level
$00:9341 87 A0        .dw LoadMapGameMode             ; 0C - Load overworld
$00:9343 6F 9F        .dw $9F6F                       ; 0D - Fade into overworld
$00:9345 BE A1        .dw $A1BE                       ; 0E - On overworld
$00:9347 37 9F        .dw TmpFade                     ; 0F - Fade to level
$00:9349 8E 96        .dw $968E                       ; 10 - Delay between overworld and Mario Start
$00:934B D5 96        .dw MarioStartGameMode          ; 11 - Mario Start screen
$00:934D 9C A5        .dw GM04Load                    ; 12 - Prepare level
$00:934F 37 9F        .dw TmpFade                     ; 13 - Fade into level
$00:9351 DA A1        .dw InLevelGameMode             ; 14 - In level
$00:9353 6F 9F        .dw $9F6F                       ; 15 - Fade to game over
$00:9355 50 97        .dw $9750                       ; 16 - Fade some more (game over)
$00:9357 59 97        .dw $9759                       ; 17 - Game over
$00:9359 6F 9F        .dw $9F6F                       ; 18 - Credits/cutscene: fade
$00:935B 68 94        .dw $9468                       ; 19 - Credits/cutscene
$00:935D 6F 9F        .dw $9F6F                       ; 1A - Credits/cutscene: fade
$00:935F FD 94        .dw $94FD                       ; 1B - Ending
$00:9361 6F 9F        .dw $9F6F                       ; 1C - Fade to Yoshi's house
$00:9363 83 95        .dw $9583                       ; 1D - Load/prepare Yoshi's house
$00:9365 6F 9F        .dw $9F6F                       ; 1E - Fade into Yoshi's house
$00:9367 AB 95        .dw $95AB                       ; 1F - Yoshi's house in the ending
$00:9369 6F 9F        .dw $9F6F                       ; 20 - Fade to enemy parade
$00:936B BC 95        .dw $95BC                       ; 21 - Load enemy parade (part 1)
$00:936D 6F 9F        .dw $9F6F                       ; 22 - Fade (enemy parade)
$00:936F C1 95        .dw $95C1                       ; 23 - Load enemy parade (part 2)
$00:9371 6F 9F        .dw $9F6F                       ; 24 - Fade into enemy parade
$00:9373 2C 96        .dw $962C                       ; 25 - Enemy parade
$00:9375 6F 9F        .dw $9F6F                       ; 26 - Fade to THE END
$00:9377 3D 96        .dw $963D                       ; 27 - Load THE END
$00:9379 7C 9F        .dw $9F7C                       ; 28 - Fade into THE END
$00:937B 8D 96        .dw $968D                       ; 29 - END (return)


;;; $937D: Turn off NMI, IRQ, HDMA and screen (TurnOffIO) ;;;
;; NMITIMEN = 0, HDMA off, force blank. Called from the start of most game modes.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:85FA: Upload stripe image to VRAM (LoadScrnImage)
;;     $00:959B: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal)
;;     $00:A087: Game mode 0C: load overworld (LoadMapGameMode)
$00:937D 9C 00 42     STZ.W $4200                     ; Disable NMI, IRQs and joypad auto-read
$00:9380 9C 0C 42     STZ.W $420C                     ; Disable all HDMA channels
$00:9383 A9 80        LDA.B #$80                      ; \
$00:9385 8D 00 21     STA.W $2100                     ; / INIDISP = $80: force blank
$00:9388 60           RTS                             ; Return



;;; $9389: Table: Nintendo logo sprite X positions (NintendoPos) ;;;
$00:9389              .db $60,$70,$80,$90             ; X positions of the four Nintendo logo sprites


;;; $938D: Game mode 00: load Nintendo Presents (NintendoTile) ;;;
;; First the logo tile table. Code: clears the screen, loads graphics and palette, builds four 16x16 logo
;;     sprites at Y = $70 (X from NintendoPos,
;; tiles from this table), starts the [$1DF5] timer at $40, sets full brightness, makes the backdrop black and
;;     moves on to game mode 01.
$00:938D              .db $02,$04,$06,$08             ; Tiles of the four Nintendo logo sprites ($02, $04, $06, $08)
; |                                                    |
; V This loads the "Nintendo Presents" and handles it. V
$00:9391 20 FA 85     JSR.W $85FA                     ; Turn off I/O, clear BG3 and hide sprites ($85FA)
$00:9394 20 79 8A     JSR.W SetUpScreen               ; Reset the BG layer addresses and screen settings (SetUpScreen)
$00:9397 20 93 A9     JSR.W $A993                     ; Load the graphics for this screen ($A993)
$00:939A A0 0C        LDY.B #$0C                      ; Y = $0C: OAM offset of sprite 3
$00:939C A2 03        LDX.B #$03                      ; X = 3: four logo sprites
$00:939E BD 89 93     LDA.W NintendoPos,X             ; \
$00:93A1 99 00 02     STA.W OAM_ExtendedDispX,Y       ; / Sprite X = NintendoPos[X]
$00:93A4 A9 70        LDA.B #$70                      ; \
$00:93A6 99 01 02     STA.W OAM_ExtendedDispY,Y       ; / Sprite Y = $70
$00:93A9 BD 8D 93     LDA.W NintendoTile,X            ; \
$00:93AC 99 02 02     STA.W OAM_ExtendedTile,Y        ; / Sprite tile = NintendoTile[X]
$00:93AF A9 30        LDA.B #$30                      ; \
$00:93B1 99 03 02     STA.W OAM_ExtendedProp,Y        ; / Properties = $30 (priority 3, palette 0)
$00:93B4 88           DEY                             ; \
$00:93B5 88           DEY                             ; |
$00:93B6 88           DEY                             ; |
$00:93B7 88           DEY                             ; / Y -= 4: previous OAM slot
$00:93B8 CA           DEX                             ; X--
$00:93B9 10 E3        BPL $939E                       ; Loop for the four sprites
$00:93BB A9 AA        LDA.B #$AA                      ; \
$00:93BD 8D 00 04     STA.W $0400                     ; / OAM size bits of sprites 0-3 = $AA: all four are 16x16
$00:93C0 A9 01        LDA.B #$01                      ; \
$00:93C2 8D FC 1D     STA.W $1DFC                     ; / Sound request [$1DFC] = 1 (the logo jingle, probably)
$00:93C5 A9 40        LDA.B #$40                      ; \
$00:93C7 8D F5 1D     STA.W $1DF5                     ; / [$1DF5] = $40: frames the screen stays up
$00:93CA A9 0F        LDA.B #$0F                      ; \
$00:93CC 8D AE 0D     STA.W $0DAE                     ; / Brightness [$0DAE] = $0F (full)
$00:93CF A9 01        LDA.B #$01                      ; \
$00:93D1 8D AF 0D     STA.W $0DAF                     ; / [$0DAF] = 1: mosaic fade direction (probably fading in)
$00:93D4 9C 2E 19     STZ.W $192E                     ; Sprite palette setting [$192E] = 0
$00:93D7 20 ED AB     JSR.W LoadPalette               ; Load the palettes (LoadPalette)
$00:93DA 9C 01 07     STZ.W $0701                     ; \
$00:93DD 9C 02 07     STZ.W $0702                     ; / Backdrop color mirror [$0701] = $0000 (black)
$00:93E0 20 2F 92     JSR.W NintenDMAINIT             ; Set CGRAM color 0 to black by DMA (NintenDMAINIT)
$00:93E3 9C 92 1B     STZ.W $1B92                     ; [$1B92] = 0: menu cursor position
$00:93E6 A2 10        LDX.B #$10                      ; X = $10: main screen shows sprites only
$00:93E8 A0 04        LDY.B #$04                      ; Y = $04: sub screen shows BG3
$00:93EA A9 01        LDA.B #$01                      ; \
$00:93EC 8D 9B 0D     STA.W $0D9B                     ; / [$0D9B] = 1: special level mode (bit 0 = no status bar)
$00:93EF A9 20        LDA.B #$20                      ; A = $20: CGADSUB value
$00:93F1 20 FD 93     JSR.W ScreenSettings            ; Apply the screen settings (ScreenSettings)
$00:93F4 EE 00 01     INC.W RAM_GameMode              ; Game mode = 1 (Nintendo Presents screen); falls into Mode04Finish

;;; $93F7: Enable NMI and joypad, return (Mode04Finish) ;;;
;; Reached by falling through from the game mode increment at $0093F4. Writes NMITIMEN = $81.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:9749: Game mode 11: Mario Start, level music (MarioStartGameMode)
;;     $00:9AC5: Detect connected controllers into [$0DA0] (SetUp0DA0GM4)
;;     $00:A0AD: Game mode 0C: load overworld (LoadMapGameMode)
$00:93F7 A9 81        LDA.B #$81                      ; \
$00:93F9 8D 00 42     STA.W $4200                     ; / NMITIMEN = $81: NMI and joypad auto-read on, no IRQs
$00:93FC 60           RTS                             ; Return


;;; $93FD: Set screen layers; game modes 01 and 06 (ScreenSettings) ;;;
;; $0093FD: sets CGADSUB (A, also mirrored in [$40]), main screen layers (X), sub screen layers (Y) and clears
;;     the window mask designation. Returns.
;; $00940F (game mode 01): counts [$1DF5] down, then decompresses Mario graphics and goes to game mode 02.
;; $00941B (game mode 06): title screen circle effect. Each frame the circle size [$1433] grows by 4 until $F0
;;     and is drawn into the window HDMA table (centre $80,$70);
;; pressing a button jumps to the final size $EC and finishes title screen setup.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:93F1: Game mode 00: load Nintendo Presents (NintendoTile)
;;     $00:A11D: Game mode 0C: load overworld (LoadMapGameMode)
$00:93FD 8D 31 21     STA.W $2131                     ; \
$00:9400 85 40        STA $40                         ; / CGADSUB ($2131) and its mirror [$40] = A
$00:9402 8E 2C 21     STX.W $212C                     ; Main screen designation ($212C) = X
$00:9405 8C 2D 21     STY.W $212D                     ; Sub screen designation ($212D) = Y
$00:9408 9C 2E 21     STZ.W $212E                     ; \
$00:940B 9C 2F 21     STZ.W $212F                     ; / Window mask designation for main and sub screen ($212E, $212F) = 0
$00:940E 60           RTS                             ; Return

$00:940F CE F5 1D     DEC.W $1DF5                     ; [$1DF5]--: Nintendo Presents timer
$00:9412 D0 06        BNE $941A                       ; Not zero yet: return
$00:9414 20 88 B8     JSR.W $B888                     ; Decompress Mario's graphics to $7E:2000 and prepare them ($B888)
$00:9417 EE 00 01     INC.W RAM_GameMode              ; Game mode += 1 (also used as a common exit by other modes)
$00:941A 60           RTS                             ; Return

; |
; V part of the "prepare title screen" code?
$00:941B 20 74 9A     JSR.W SetUp0DA0GM4              ; Choose which controller is used (SetUp0DA0GM4)
$00:941E 20 BE 9C     JSR.W $9CBE                     ; Check for button presses; Z = none ($9CBE)
$00:9421 F0 0B        BEQ $942E                       ; No button pressed: go on with the circle ($00942E)
$00:9423 A9 EC        LDA.B #$EC                      ; A = $EC: final circle size
$00:9425 20 40 94     JSR.W $9440                     ; Store it and draw the circle ($9440)
$00:9428 EE 00 01     INC.W RAM_GameMode              ; Game mode += 1
$00:942B 4C 9F 9C     JMP.W $9C9F                     ; Finish title screen setup and return ($9C9F)

$00:942E CE F5 1D     DEC.W $1DF5                     ; [$1DF5]-- (title timer, also the demo controller timer)
$00:9431 D0 E7        BNE $941A                       ; Not zero: return
$00:9433 EE F5 1D     INC.W $1DF5                     ; Undo the decrement
$00:9436 AD 33 14     LDA.W $1433                     ; \
$00:9439 18           CLC                             ; |
$00:943A 69 04        ADC.B #$04                      ; |
$00:943C C9 F0        CMP.B #$F0                      ; |
$00:943E B0 D7        BCS $9417                       ; / Circle size [$1433] + 4; if >= $F0 the effect is done: next game mode
$00:9440 8D 33 14     STA.W $1433                     ; Store the new circle size in [$1433]
$00:9443 20 61 CA     JSR.W $CA61                     ; Point [$04] and [$06] at the circle data $CB12 ($CA61)
$00:9446 A9 80        LDA.B #$80                      ; \
$00:9448 85 00        STA $00                         ; |
$00:944A A9 70        LDA.B #$70                      ; |
$00:944C 85 01        STA $01                         ; / Circle centre: [$00] = $80 (X), [$01] = $70 (Y)
$00:944E 4C 88 CA     JMP.W $CA88                     ; Draw the circle into the window HDMA table and return ($CA88)



;;; $9451: Table: cutscene background settings (CutsceneBgColor) ;;;
;; Indexed by cutscene number - 1; value goes to [$192F] when a cutscene is loaded.
$00:9451              .db $02,$00,$04,$01,$00,$06,$04 ; Cutscene 1-7 background color setting for [$192F] (indexed by cutscene number - 1)


;;; $9458: Cutscene, ending and game mode code (castle scenes, credits, game over) (CutsceneCastlePal) ;;;
;; Table data, then the game mode routines for modes 03, 10, 11, 16, 17, 19, 1B, 1D, 1F, 21, 23, 25 and 27
;;     plus helpers.
;; $009458/$009460: palette and border image tables indexed by cutscene number [$13C6]. $009468: mode 19 (load
;;     castle cutscene or credits).
;; $0094FD: mode 1B (cutscene frame; mode 19 also runs it once). $00955E: decompress GFX file $2F and copy
;;     $0200 words to VRAM $4600.
;; $009583/$0095BC/$0095C1/$00962C/$00963D: ending modes (Yoshi's House, enemy parade, THE END). $009622:
;;     shared tail setting main/sub screen and advancing the mode.
;; $00968E: mode 10. $0096AE: mode 03 (load title screen; falls into the mode 11 body). $00974C: JSL wrapper
;;     for HexToDec.
;; $009750: mode 16. $009759: mode 17 (game over). Quirk: many ending routines have unresolved purposes (calls
;;     into bank $0C).
$00:9458              .db $03,$06,$05,$06,$03,$03,$06,$06 ; Castle palette for each cutscene, indexed by [$13C6] (entry 0 unused)
$00:9460              .db $03,$FF,$FF,$C9,$0F,$FF,$CC,$C9 ; Stripe image number for each cutscene's border graphics, indexed by [$13C6]

$00:9468 20 FA 85     JSR.W $85FA                     ; Turn off NMI/IRQ/HDMA and screen, clear BG3 and sprites ($85FA)
$00:946B 20 A6 A1     JSR.W Clear_1A_13D3             ; Clear layer scroll positions and [$13D3] (Clear_1A_13D3)
$00:946E 20 79 8A     JSR.W SetUpScreen               ; Set up the screen (SetUpScreen)
$00:9471 AE C6 13     LDX.W $13C6                     ; X = cutscene number [$13C6] (1-7 castle scenes, 8 = credits)
$00:9474 A9 18        LDA.B #$18                      ; \
$00:9476 8D 31 19     STA.W $1931                     ; / Tileset [$1931] = $18 (cutscene castle)
$00:9479 A9 14        LDA.B #$14                      ; \
$00:947B 8D 2B 19     STA.W $192B                     ; / Sprite GFX set [$192B] = $14
$00:947E BD 50 94     LDA.W CutsceneBgColor-1,X       ; \
$00:9481 8D 2F 19     STA.W $192F                     ; |
$00:9484 BD 58 94     LDA.W CutsceneCastlePal,X       ; } Background color setting [$192F] and castle palette [$1930] for this cutscene
$00:9487 8D 30 19     STA.W $1930                     ; /
$00:948A 9C 2E 19     STZ.W $192E                     ; Sprite palette setting [$192E] = 0
$00:948D A9 01        LDA.B #$01                      ; \
$00:948F 8D 2D 19     STA.W $192D                     ; / FG palette setting [$192D] = 1 (brown/cream)
$00:9492 E0 08        CPX.B #$08                      ; \
$00:9494 D0 1C        BNE $94B2                       ; / Not the credits (cutscene 8)? Then go load a castle scene
$00:9496 20 5E 95     JSR.W $955E                     ; Decompress GFX file $2F and copy $0200 words to VRAM $4600 ($955E)
$00:9499 A9 D2        LDA.B #$D2                      ; \
$00:949B 85 12        STA $12                         ; / Stripe image $D2 (credits background)
$00:949D 20 D2 85     JSR.W LoadScrnImage             ; Upload the stripe image (LoadScrnImage)
$00:94A0 20 59 81     JSR.W UploadMusicBank3          ; Upload music bank 3 (ending music)
$00:94A3 22 DD 93 0C  JSL.L $93DD                     ; Credits setup in bank $0C ($93DD)
$00:94A7 20 60 92     JSR.W $9260                     ; Clear all HDMA ($9260)
$00:94AA EE 31 19     INC.W $1931                     ; \
$00:94AD EE 2B 19     INC.W $192B                     ; / Credits use the next tileset [$1931] and sprite GFX set [$192B]
$00:94B0 80 25        BRA $94D7                       ; Continue at $0094D7

$00:94B2 A9 15        LDA.B #$15                      ; \
$00:94B4 8D FB 1D     STA.W $1DFB                     ; / Music request [$1DFB] = $15 (cutscene music)
$00:94B7 BD 60 94     LDA.W $9460,X                   ; \
$00:94BA 85 12        STA $12                         ; } Upload this cutscene's border stripe image from $009460[X]
$00:94BC 20 D2 85     JSR.W LoadScrnImage             ; /
$00:94BF A9 CF        LDA.B #$CF                      ; \
$00:94C1 85 12        STA $12                         ; } Upload stripe image $CF as well
$00:94C3 20 D2 85     JSR.W LoadScrnImage             ; /
$00:94C6 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$00:94C8 A9 90 00     LDA.W #$0090                    ; \
$00:94CB 85 94        STA RAM_MarioXPos               ; |
$00:94CD A9 58 00     LDA.W #$0058                    ; } Mario position = ($0090, $0058)
$00:94D0 85 96        STA RAM_MarioYPos               ; /
$00:94D2 E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$00:94D4 EE 8F 14     INC.W $148F                     ; [$148F]++ (Mario carrying flag; purpose here unclear)
$00:94D7 20 DA A9     JSR.W UploadSpriteGFX           ; Upload sprite graphics set [$192B] (UploadSpriteGFX)
$00:94DA 20 ED AB     JSR.W LoadPalette               ; Load the palettes (LoadPalette)
$00:94DD 20 2F 92     JSR.W $922F                     ; Set up the CGRAM DMA for the palette buffer ($922F)
$00:94E0 A2 0B        LDX.B #$0B                      ; \
$00:94E2 74 1A        STZ RAM_ScreenBndryXLo,X        ; |
$00:94E4 CA           DEX                             ; } Clear layer positions [$1A]-[$25]: every layer scrolled to 0
$00:94E5 10 FB        BPL $94E2                       ; /
$00:94E7 A9 20        LDA.B #$20                      ; \
$00:94E9 85 64        STA $64                         ; / [$64] = $20: sprite priority bits for the scene
$00:94EB 20 35 A6     JSR.W $A635                     ; Adjust music for active power-ups ($A635)
$00:94EE 64 76        STZ RAM_MarioDirection          ; Mario faces right
$00:94F0 64 72        STZ RAM_IsFlying                ; Mario is not flying
$00:94F2 22 B1 CE 00  JSL.L $CEB1                     ; Mario init routine in bank $00 ($CEB1)
$00:94F6 A2 17        LDX.B #$17                      ; X = $17: main screen BG1, BG2, BG3, OBJ
$00:94F8 A0 00        LDY.B #$00                      ; Y = 0: no sub screen layers
$00:94FA 20 22 96     JSR.W $9622                     ; Apply screen settings, BGMODE mirror and advance game mode ($9622)
$00:94FD 22 00 80 7F  JSL.L RAM_7F8000                ; Game mode 1B entry: move all sprites off-screen

;;; $96D5: Game mode 11: Mario Start, level music (MarioStartGameMode) ;;;
;; Entered at $0096D5. Disables NMI, clears buttons, optionally shows the Mario Start message, resets
;;     overworld processing, copies layer positions,
;; loads the level data ($801E), picks the level music request ([$1DFB]/[$0DDA]), blacks the screen and
;;     advances the game mode.
;; $0097BC: Mode 7 boss room setup (called from level load): sets up screen, sprite GFX, window masks and
;;     Mario for the boss room; $009801 is the non-bit-6 variant.
$00:96D5 9C 00 42     STZ.W $4200                     ; Game mode 11: disable NMI, IRQ and joypad reading
$00:96D8 20 2D F6     JSR.W NoButtons                 ; Clear the controller inputs (NoButtons)
$00:96DB AD 1A 14     LDA.W $141A                     ; \

$00:96E0 AD 1D 14     LDA.W $141D                     ; \
$00:96E3 F0 04        BEQ $96E9                       ; / [$141D] zero: skip showing the message
$00:96E5 22 09 DC 04  JSL.L $DC09                     ; Mario Start message setup in bank $04 ($DC09)
$00:96E9 9C D5 13     STZ.W $13D5                     ; [$13D5] = 0
$00:96EC 9C D9 13     STZ.W $13D9                     ; [$13D9] = 0: stop overworld processing
$00:96EF A9 50        LDA.B #$50                      ; \
$00:96F1 8D D6 13     STA.W $13D6                     ; / [$13D6] = $50
$00:96F4 22 96 D7 05  JSL.L $D796                     ; Level/overworld setup in bank $05 ($D796)
$00:96F8 A2 07        LDX.B #$07                      ; X = 7
$00:96FA B5 1A        LDA RAM_ScreenBndryXLo,X        ; \
$00:96FC 9D 62 14     STA.W $1462,X                   ; / Copy layer positions [$1A]-[$21] to $1462-$1469 (previous positions)
$00:96FF CA           DEX                             ; Next byte
$00:9700 10 F8        BPL $96FA                       ; Loop for 8 bytes
$00:9702 20 34 81     JSR.W $8134                     ; Upload level music bank if needed ($8134)
$00:9705 20 35 A6     JSR.W $A635                     ; Adjust music for active power-ups ($A635)
$00:9708 A9 20        LDA.B #$20                      ; \
$00:970A 85 5E        STA $5E                         ; / [$5E] = $20
$00:970C 20 96 A7     JSR.W $A796                     ; $A796
$00:970F EE 04 14     INC.W $1404                     ; [$1404]++ (layer 1 vertical scroll flag)

$00:971A AD 09 01     LDA.W $0109                     ; \
$00:971D F0 09        BEQ $9728                       ; / [$0109] = 0: skip to the music check
$00:971F C9 E9        CMP.B #$E9                      ; \
$00:9721 D0 1D        BNE $9740                       ; / [$0109] != $E9 (intro level): skip the music setup
$00:9723 A9 13        LDA.B #$13                      ; \
$00:9725 8D DA 0D     STA.W $0DDA                     ; / Music number [$0DDA] = $13 (intro level)
$00:9728 AD DA 0D     LDA.W $0DDA                     ; A = [$0DDA] (level music number)
$00:972B C9 40        CMP.B #$40                      ; Bit 6 / value >= $40: music already requested
$00:972D B0 0C        BCS $973B                       ; Skip the request
$00:972F AC 9B 0D     LDY.W $0D9B                     ; Y = [$0D9B] (special level mode)
$00:9732 C0 C1        CPY.B #$C1                      ; \
$00:9734 D0 02        BNE $9738                       ; / Y = $C1 (Bowser fight)?

$00:973D 8D DA 0D     STA.W $0DDA                     ; / Remove bit 6 from the music number and store it in [$0DDA]
$00:9740 9C AE 0D     STZ.W $0DAE                     ; Brightness mirror [$0DAE] = 0 (black)

$00:978B 38           SEC                             ; \
$00:978C E9 04        SBC.B #$04                      ; / A -= 4 (move the animation)
$00:978E 8D 3C 14     STA.W $143C                     ; [$143C] = A
$00:9791 18           CLC                             ; \
$00:9792 69 A0        ADC.B #$A0                      ; } [$00] = [$143C] + $A0 (X position of the first tile)
$00:9794 85 00        STA $00                         ; /
$00:9796 26 01        ROL $01                         ; [$01] = carry (high byte)
$00:9798 AE 3B 14     LDX.W $143B                     ; X = [$143B] (tile index)

$00:97A1 A9 78        LDA.B #$78                      ; \
$00:97A3 38           SEC                             ; |
$00:97A4 ED 3C 14     SBC.W $143C                     ; |
$00:97A7 85 00        STA $00                         ; |
$00:97A9 2A           ROL                             ; |
$00:97AA 49 01        EOR.B #$01                      ; } Mirrored position: [$00] = $78 - [$143C], [$01] = high byte XOR 1
$00:97AC 85 01        STA $01                         ; /
$00:97AE 20 E9 91     JSR.W $91E9                     ; Draw a pair of tiles in OAM ($91E9)

$00:97B2 98           TYA                             ; \

;;     $00:9A8B: Detect connected controllers into [$0DA0] (SetUp0DA0GM4)
;;     $00:9ACC: Menu cursor handler
;;     $00:9C64: Game mode 07: title screen and demo (GAMEMODE_07)
;;     $00:A1BE: Clear RAM; game mode 0E: overworld (Clear_1A_13D3)
$00:9A74 AD 16 40     LDA.W $4016                     ; Read controller 1 data line: bit 0 = connected
$00:9A77 4A           LSR                             ; Bit 0 into carry
$00:9A78 AD 17 40     LDA.W $4017                     ; Read controller 2 data line
$00:9A7B 2A           ROL                             ; Controller 2 bit in bit 1, controller 1 bit in bit 0
$00:9A7C 29 03        AND.B #$03                      ; Bit 0 = controller 1 connected, bit 1 = controller 2 connected
$00:9A7E F0 07        BEQ $9A87                       ; None connected: use controller 1 data (index 0)
$00:9A80 C9 03        CMP.B #$03                      ; \
$00:9A82 D0 02        BNE $9A86                       ; / Both connected?
$00:9A84 09 80        ORA.B #$80                      ; Both connected: set bit 7 (use the current player's controller)
$00:9A86 3A           DEC A                           ; Index of the controller to use: 0 = controller 1, 1 = controller 2
$00:9A87 8D A0 0D     STA.W $0DA0                     ; [$0DA0] = index (negative = current player)
$00:9A8A 60           RTS                             ; Return

$00:9A8B 20 74 9A     JSR.W SetUp0DA0GM4              ; Game mode 04: set up [$0DA0] (SetUp0DA0GM4)
$00:9A8E 20 9C A5     JSR.W GM04Load                  ; Load the level (GM04Load)
$00:9A91 9C 31 0F     STZ.W $0F31                     ; Level timer [$0F31] = 0
$00:9A94 20 FA 85     JSR.W $85FA                     ; Clear BG3 and sprites ($85FA)
$00:9A97 A9 03        LDA.B #$03                      ; \
$00:9A99 85 12        STA $12                         ; / Stripe image $03 (title screen)
$00:9A9B 20 D2 85     JSR.W LoadScrnImage             ; Upload the stripe image (LoadScrnImage)
$00:9A9E 20 A6 AD     JSR.W $ADA6                     ; $ADA6
$00:9AA1 20 2F 92     JSR.W $922F                     ; Set up the CGRAM DMA for the palette buffer ($922F)
$00:9AA4 22 75 F6 04  JSL.L $F675                     ; Title screen code in bank $04 ($F675)
$00:9AA8 A9 01        LDA.B #$01                      ; \
$00:9AAA 8D 9B 0D     STA.W $0D9B                     ; / Special level mode [$0D9B] = 1
$00:9AAD A9 33        LDA.B #$33                      ; \
$00:9AAF 85 41        STA $41                         ; / Window mask mirror [$41] = $33
$00:9AB1 A9 00        LDA.B #$00                      ; \
$00:9AB3 85 42        STA $42                         ; / Window mask mirror [$42] = $00
$00:9AB5 A9 23        LDA.B #$23                      ; \
$00:9AB7 85 43        STA $43                         ; / Window mask mirror [$43] = $23
$00:9AB9 A9 12        LDA.B #$12                      ; \
$00:9ABB 85 44        STA $44                         ; / Color math mirror [$44] = $12
$00:9ABD 20 43 94     JSR.W $9443                     ; Set up the title circle HDMA ($9443)
$00:9AC0 A9 10        LDA.B #$10                      ; \
$00:9AC2 8D F5 1D     STA.W $1DF5                     ; / [$1DF5] = $10 (purpose unclear)
$00:9AC5 4C F7 93     JMP.W Mode04Finish              ; Enable NMI and joypad and return (Mode04Finish)



;;; $9AC8..9AC8: Table: menu cursor movement ;;;
;; +1 (Down), -1 (Up), -1 (both).
$00:9AC8              .db $01,$FF,$FF                 ; Cursor movement: +1 for Down, -1 for Up, -1 for both


;;; $9ACB: Menu cursor handler ;;;
;; Reads D-pad, Select and A/B/Start, moves cursor [$1B92] within [$8A] entries (wraps), plays sounds via
;;     [$1DFC].
;; Quirk: returns twice (pops the caller's return address) unless B, Start or A is pressed.
;; Parameters: Y: cursor graphics parameter passed to $9E82.
;; Called by:
;;     $00:9CDD: Game mode 08: file select, mode 0A: players
;;     $00:9E0A: Game mode 08: file select, mode 0A: players
$00:9ACB 5A           PHY                             ; Menu cursor handler: save Y (cursor graphics parameter)
$00:9ACC 20 74 9A     JSR.W SetUp0DA0GM4              ; Read the controller setup (SetUp0DA0GM4)
$00:9ACF 7A           PLY                             ; Restore Y
$00:9AD0 EE 91 1B     INC.W $1B91                     ; [$1B91]++ (cursor blink counter)
$00:9AD3 20 82 9E     JSR.W $9E82                     ; Draw the cursor ($9E82)
$00:9AD6 AE 92 1B     LDX.W $1B92                     ; X = [$1B92] (current cursor position)
$00:9AD9 A5 16        LDA $16                         ; \
$00:9ADB 29 90        AND.B #$90                      ; / New B or Start press ([$16] AND $90)?
$00:9ADD D0 04        BNE $9AE3                       ; Yes: confirm
$00:9ADF A5 18        LDA $18                         ; A = [$18] (new A press)
$00:9AE1 10 07        BPL $9AEA                       ; Not pressed: go handle the D-pad
$00:9AE3 A9 01        LDA.B #$01                      ; \
$00:9AE5 8D FC 1D     STA.W $1DFC                     ; / Sound request [$1DFC] = 1 (confirm)
$00:9AE8 80 27        BRA $9B11                       ; Go reset the cursor position

$00:9AEA 68           PLA                             ; Pop the return address: skip the caller's confirm code
$00:9AEB 68           PLA                             ; (second PLA)
$00:9AEC A5 16        LDA $16                         ; \
$00:9AEE 29 20        AND.B #$20                      ; / A = new presses ([$16]) AND $20 (Select)
$00:9AF0 4A           LSR                             ; Shift Select into the Down bit
$00:9AF1 4A           LSR                             ; (shift)
$00:9AF2 4A           LSR                             ; (shift)
$00:9AF3 05 16        ORA $16                         ; Combine with the D-pad bits
$00:9AF5 29 0C        AND.B #$0C                      ; Keep Down ($04) and Up ($08)
$00:9AF7 F0 1D        BEQ $9B16                       ; Neither pressed: return to the caller's caller
$00:9AF9 A0 06        LDY.B #$06                      ; \
$00:9AFB 8C FC 1D     STY.W $1DFC                     ; / Sound request [$1DFC] = 6 (cursor move)
$00:9AFE 9C 91 1B     STZ.W $1B91                     ; Reset the blink counter
$00:9B01 4A           LSR                             ; Shift the direction bits
$00:9B02 4A           LSR                             ; (shift)
$00:9B03 A8           TAY                             ; Y = 1 (Down), 2 (Up) or 3 (both)
$00:9B04 8A           TXA                             ; A = old cursor position
$00:9B05 79 C7 9A     ADC.W $9AC8-1,Y                 ; Add the movement from $9AC8-1[Y]
$00:9B08 10 03        BPL $9B0D                       ; Not negative: check the upper limit
$00:9B0A A5 8A        LDA $8A                         ; Negative: wrap to the last entry, [$8A] - 1
$00:9B0C 3A           DEC A                           ; (decrement)
$00:9B0D C5 8A        CMP $8A                         ; New position < [$8A] (number of entries)?
$00:9B0F 90 02        BCC $9B13                       ; Yes: keep it
$00:9B11 A9 00        LDA.B #$00                      ; Position = 0 (wrap to the first entry, or reset after confirm)
$00:9B13 8D 92 1B     STA.W $1B92                     ; [$1B92] = new cursor position
$00:9B16 60           RTS                             ; Return



;;; $9B17..9B17: Unused data (3 bytes) ;;;
$00:9B17              .db $04,$02,$01                 ; Unused data (3 bytes)


;;; $9B1A: Game mode 09: erase file menu ;;;
;; Game mode 09. Draws the ERASE DATA screen on top of the file select. The cursor chooses files (marking them
;;     in [$0DDE], bit 2 = file 0,
;; bit 0 = file 2) or END. On END, all marked files are cleared from both SRAM copies. Y or X cancels back to
;;     file select.
;; $009B80: long-call wrapper (called from the overworld in bank $04) that runs the CONTINUE/END menu for
;;     state [$13C9] - 1.
$00:9B1A C2 20        REP #$20                        ; \
$00:9B1C A9 C9 39     LDA.W #$39C9                    ; |
$00:9B1F A0 60        LDY.B #$60                      ; } BG color = $39C9, CGADSUB = $60 ($9D30)
$00:9B21 20 30 9D     JSR.W $9D30                     ; /
$00:9B24 A5 16        LDA $16                         ; A = buttons just pressed on controller 1 ([$16])
$00:9B26 05 18        ORA $18                         ; Or in controller 2's ([$18])
$00:9B28 29 40        AND.B #$40                      ; Keep bit 6 (Y on pad 1, X on pad 2): the cancel buttons
$00:9B2A F0 0C        BEQ $9B38                       ; Not pressed: go handle the menu
$00:9B2C CE 00 01     DEC.W RAM_GameMode              ; \
$00:9B2F CE 00 01     DEC.W RAM_GameMode              ; / Game mode -= 2 (back to file select; $9CB0 increments once)
$00:9B32 20 11 9B     JSR.W $9B11                     ; Cursor position [$1B92] = 0 ($9B11)
$00:9B35 4C B0 9C     JMP.W $9CB0                     ; Rebuild the file select screen and move on

$00:9B38 A0 08        LDY.B #$08                      ; Y = 8: 4 menu entries (3 files + END)
$00:9B3A 20 D0 9A     JSR.W $9AD0                     ; Move the cursor / wait for a selection (returns X = entry only on selection)
$00:9B3D E0 03        CPX.B #$03                      ; Entry 3 (END) selected?
$00:9B3F D0 2C        BNE $9B6D                       ; No: a file was toggled, go mark it
$00:9B41 A0 02        LDY.B #$02                      ; Y = 2: start with file 2, loop down to file 0
$00:9B43 4E DE 0D     LSR.W $0DDE                     ; Shift marked-for-erase bits [$0DDE]; carry = this file is marked
$00:9B46 90 1F        BCC $9B67                       ; Not marked: next file
$00:9B48 5A           PHY                             ; Save file number
$00:9B49 B9 CB 9C     LDA.W $9CCB,Y                   ; A = high byte of this file's SRAM offset
$00:9B4C EB           XBA                             ; Move it to the high half of A
$00:9B4D B9 CE 9C     LDA.W $9CCE,Y                   ; A = low byte of the offset
$00:9B50 C2 10        REP #$10                        ; Index registers 16-bit
$00:9B52 AA           TAX                             ; X = SRAM offset of the file
$00:9B53 A0 8F 00     LDY.W #$008F                    ; Y = $008F: bytes per file slot
$00:9B56 A9 00        LDA.B #$00                      ; Fill value = 0
$00:9B58 9F 00 00 70  STA.L $700000,X                 ; Clear a byte of the primary copy at $70:0000+X
$00:9B5C 9F AD 01 70  STA.L $7001AD,X                 ; Clear the same byte of the backup copy ($1AD bytes later)
$00:9B60 E8           INX                             ; Next byte
$00:9B61 88           DEY                             ; Count down
$00:9B62 D0 F4        BNE $9B58                       ; Repeat for the whole slot
$00:9B64 E2 10        SEP #$10                        ; Index registers 8-bit
$00:9B66 7A           PLY                             ; Restore file number
$00:9B67 88           DEY                             ; Next file
$00:9B68 10 D9        BPL $9B43                       ; Loop for files 2, 1, 0
$00:9B6A 4C 89 9C     JMP.W $9C89                     ; Erase done: game mode = 2 (back to the title screen)

$00:9B6D 8E 92 1B     STX.W $1B92                     ; Cursor position [$1B92] = file
$00:9B70 BD 17 9B     LDA.W $9B17,X                   ; A = bit for this file ($04, $02, $01)
$00:9B73 0D DE 0D     ORA.W $0DDE                     ; \
$00:9B76 8D DE 0D     STA.W $0DDE                     ; / [$0DDE] |= file bit (file is marked for erasing)
$00:9B79 85 05        STA $05                         ; Pass the marked bits to the tilemap code in [$05]
$00:9B7B A2 00        LDX.B #$00                      ; X = 0: erase-menu stripe data offset
$00:9B7D 4C 3C 9D     JMP.W $9D3C                     ; Rebuild the menu tilemap (marked files show EMPTY)

$00:9B80 8B           PHB                             ; \
$00:9B81 4B           PHK                             ; } Data bank = $00 (wrapper for the long call from bank $04)
$00:9B82 AB           PLB                             ; /
$00:9B83 20 88 9B     JSR.W $9B88                     ; Run the Continue/End game over menu
$00:9B86 AB           PLB                             ; Restore data bank
$00:9B87 6B           RTL                             ; Return long

$00:9B88 3A           DEC A                           ; A = [$13C9] - 1 (menu state)
$00:9B89 22 DF 86 00  JSL.L ExecutePtr                ; Run the routine for the state (ExecutePtr)


;;; $9B8D: Pointer table: Continue/End menu, save prompt (Ptrs009B8D) ;;;
;; $009B8D: pointers for [$13C9] = 1 (draw CONTINUE/END) and 2 (run the menu: CONTINUE resets lives, END
;;     returns to the title).
;; $009BA8: wrapper for the overworld save prompt; entry 0 saves the game with the jingle ($1DF9 = 5), then
;;     closes the prompt.
;; $009BC9: save game routine. Copies $8D bytes from $1F49 to the file's SRAM slot at $70:xxxx plus a 16-bit
;;     checksum ($5A5A - sum),
;; and writes the same to the backup copy $1AD bytes later. Parameters: [$010A] = file number.
;; $009C13: closes the message box ([$1B87]++, [$1B88]++) and clears the stripe buffer with image $1B.
$00:9B8D 91 9B        .dw $9B91                       ; State 1: show the CONTINUE/END text
$00:9B8F 9A 9B        .dw $9B9A                       ; State 2: run the menu

$00:9B91 A0 0C        LDY.B #$0C                      ; Y = $0C: stripe image CONTINUE/END
$00:9B93 20 29 9D     JSR.W $9D29                     ; Show it (clears the RAM stripe buffer, [$12] = Y)
$00:9B96 EE C9 13     INC.W $13C9                     ; [$13C9]++: next state, the menu itself
$00:9B99 60           RTS                             ; Return

$00:9B9A A0 00        LDY.B #$00                      ; Y = 0: menu of 2 entries (CONTINUE, END)
$00:9B9C 20 D0 9A     JSR.W $9AD0                     ; Move the cursor (returns only when an entry is chosen)
$00:9B9F 8A           TXA                             ; A = chosen entry
$00:9BA0 D0 03        BNE $9BA5                       ; END: go to the title screen
$00:9BA2 4C 17 9E     JMP.W $9E17                     ; CONTINUE: reset the player data and go on

$00:9BA5 4C 89 9C     JMP.W $9C89                     ; Game mode = 2 (title screen)

$00:9BA8 8B           PHB                             ; \
$00:9BA9 4B           PHK                             ; } Data bank = $00 (wrapper for the long call from bank $04)
$00:9BAA AB           PLB                             ; /
$00:9BAB 20 B0 9B     JSR.W $9BB0                     ; Run the save prompt
$00:9BAE AB           PLB                             ; Restore data bank
$00:9BAF 6B           RTL                             ; Return long

$00:9BB0 A0 06        LDY.B #$06                      ; Y = 6: menu of 2 entries (save / don't save)
$00:9BB2 20 D0 9A     JSR.W $9AD0                     ; Move the cursor (returns only when an entry is chosen)
$00:9BB5 8A           TXA                             ; A = chosen entry
$00:9BB6 D0 0C        BNE $9BC4                       ; Second entry: skip saving
$00:9BB8 9C FC 1D     STZ.W $1DFC                     ; Clear the sound request port $1DFC
$00:9BBB A9 05        LDA.B #$05                      ; Sound effect $05 ...
$00:9BBD 8D F9 1D     STA.W $1DF9                     ; ... on $1DF9 (save game jingle)
$00:9BC0 22 C9 9B 00  JSL.L $9BC9                     ; Write the current game to SRAM
$00:9BC4 22 13 9C 00  JSL.L $9C13                     ; Close the prompt ($9C13)
$00:9BC8 60           RTS                             ; Return


;V Save game routine
$00:9BC9 8B           PHB                             ; \
$00:9BCA 4B           PHK                             ; } Data bank = $00
$00:9BCB AB           PLB                             ; /
$00:9BCC AE 0A 01     LDX.W $010A                     ; X = save file number ([$010A])
$00:9BCF BD CB 9C     LDA.W $9CCB,X                   ; A = high byte of this file's SRAM offset (0, 0, 1)
$00:9BD2 EB           XBA                             ; Move it to the high half of A
$00:9BD3 BD CE 9C     LDA.W $9CCE,X                   ; A = low byte of the offset (00, 8F, 1E)
$00:9BD6 C2 10        REP #$10                        ; Index registers 16-bit
$00:9BD8 AA           TAX                             ; X = SRAM offset of the file
$00:9BD9 A0 00 00     LDY.W #$0000                    ; Y = 0: index into the save data in RAM
$00:9BDC 84 8A        STY $8A                         ; Checksum sum [$8A] = 0
$00:9BDE B9 49 1F     LDA.W $1F49,Y                   ; A = byte of the save data at $1F49+Y
$00:9BE1 9F 00 00 70  STA.L $700000,X                 ; Write it to SRAM $70:0000+X
$00:9BE5 18           CLC                             ; \
$00:9BE6 65 8A        ADC $8A                         ; } [$8A] += A (16-bit running sum)
$00:9BE8 85 8A        STA $8A                         ; /
$00:9BEA 90 02        BCC $9BEE                       ; \
$00:9BEC E6 8B        INC $8B                         ; / Add the carry into [$8B]
$00:9BEE E8           INX                             ; Next SRAM byte
$00:9BEF C8           INY                             ; Next RAM byte
$00:9BF0 C0 8D 00     CPY.W #$008D                    ; All $8D bytes copied?
$00:9BF3 90 E9        BCC $9BDE                       ; No: loop
$00:9BF5 C2 20        REP #$20                        ; A 16-bit
$00:9BF7 A9 5A 5A     LDA.W #$5A5A                    ; A = $5A5A
$00:9BFA 38           SEC                             ; Set carry
$00:9BFB E5 8A        SBC $8A                         ; A = $5A5A - sum: the checksum word
$00:9BFD 9F 00 00 70  STA.L $700000,X                 ; Store it after the data (offset $8D)
$00:9C01 E0 AD 01     CPX.W #$01AD                    ; X >= $01AD? (the backup copy was just written)
$00:9C04 B0 09        BCS $9C0F                       ; Yes: finished
$00:9C06 8A           TXA                             ; A = X
$00:9C07 69 20 01     ADC.W #$0120                    ; A += $0120 (carry is clear): X = offset of the backup copy ($1AD above the primary)
$00:9C0A AA           TAX                             ; X = backup copy offset
$00:9C0B E2 20        SEP #$20                        ; A 8-bit
$00:9C0D 80 CA        BRA $9BD9                       ; Write the second copy

$00:9C0F E2 30        SEP #$30                        ; A, X and Y 8-bit
$00:9C11 AB           PLB                             ; Restore data bank
$00:9C12 6B           RTL                             ; Return long

$00:9C13 EE 87 1B     INC.W $1B87                     ; [$1B87]++ (overworld message box state: advance)
$00:9C16 EE 88 1B     INC.W $1B88                     ; [$1B88]++ (message box expanding flag)
$00:9C19 A0 1B        LDY.B #$1B                      ; Y = $1B: stripe image (replaces the prompt)


;;; $9C1B: Tail of CODE_009C13 (JSR $9D29) (Instr009C1B) ;;;
;; These bytes are the opcodes for JSR $9D29 (show stripe image Y) listed as data; the RTL after them returns
;;     from $9C13.
$00:9C1B              .db $20,$29,$9D                 ; Opcode bytes for JSR $9D29 (disassembled as data)

$00:9C1E 6B           RTL                             ; Return long



;;; $9C1F: Title demo: first buttons byte (IntroControlData) ;;;
;; Buttons for demo segment 0 (Y + Right); the segment's duration is in ItrCntrlrSqnc.
$00:9C1F              .db $41                         ; Demo script: controller 1 buttons for the first segment (Y + Right)


;;; $9C20: Title screen demo input script (ItrCntrlrSqnc) ;;;
;; Recorded controller input for the title screen demo (Mario plays the intro level by himself). Buttons and
;;     times alternate: the first
;; buttons byte is at $009C1F, then time, buttons, time, ... Buttons use the format of [$15] (B Y Select Start
;;     Up Down Left Right).
;; $FF as buttons ends the demo.
$00:9C20              .db $0F,$C1,$30,$00,$10,$42,$20,$41 ; Time/buttons alternate: [time, buttons] pairs, first time $0F
$00:9C28              .db $70,$81,$11,$00,$80,$82,$0C,$00 ; Demo script, continued
$00:9C30              .db $30,$C1,$30,$41,$60,$C1,$10,$00 ; Demo script, continued
$00:9C38              .db $40,$01,$30,$E1,$01,$00,$60,$41 ; Demo script, continued
$00:9C40              .db $4E,$80,$10,$00,$30,$41,$58,$00 ; Demo script, continued
$00:9C48              .db $20,$60,$01,$00,$30,$60,$01,$00 ; Demo script, continued
$00:9C50              .db $30,$60,$01,$00,$30,$60,$01,$00 ; Demo script, continued
$00:9C58              .db $30,$60,$01,$00,$30,$41,$1A,$C1 ; Demo script, continued
$00:9C60              .db $30,$00,$30,$FF             ; Demo script end: buttons $FF finishes the demo


;;; $9C64: Game mode 07: title screen and demo (GAMEMODE_07) ;;;
;; Runs the title screen. A press of B, Y, Select, Start, A or X ($9CBE) leaves for the file select
;;     (game mode 08).
;; Otherwise the scripted input from ItrCntrlrSqnc is fed to the controller mirrors and the level engine runs
;;     the demo.
;; When the script ends the game mode is set to 2 and the title screen restarts. $009C89 is shared as 'go to
;;     game mode 2'.
;; $009CBE: Returns: Z = clear if no button is pressed.
$00:9C64 20 74 9A     JSR.W SetUp0DA0GM4              ; Check which controllers are connected (SetUp0DA0GM4)
$00:9C67 20 BE 9C     JSR.W $9CBE                     ; Any of the buttons B, Y, Select, Start, A, X pressed? (Z = no)
$00:9C6A D0 33        BNE $9C9F                       ; Yes: leave the title screen
$00:9C6C 20 2D F6     JSR.W NoButtons                 ; Clear the controller mirrors ([$15]-[$18])
